reference_answer: Three procedures put the EAS and the EEC in the same step: the common-EAS discovery procedure for EECs connected to the same EES (TS 23.700-98 clause 7.31.2.3), where EEC-1/EEC-3 use EDN configuration information to establish a connection to the common EAS discovered via EES; the EAS instantiation-on-demand procedure (TS 23.700-98 clause 7.33.2.2), where the EEC sends an EAS selection request identifying the selected (not-yet-instantiated) EAS and later the AC accesses that EAS; and the 5GMS client-driven Edge Processing procedure (TS 26.501 clause 8.1), where the EEC discovers, requests and selects a "5GMS AS" EAS instance and registers with the serving EES.

question: For QoS flow handling in NR, which procedures put the QFI and the UPF in the same step?
reference_answer: Three procedures in TS 38.300 Annex A put the QFI and the UPF in the same step: the new QoS flow with Reflective QoS (RQoS) procedure (A.2), where the gNB receives a downlink packet carrying a new QFI from the UPF and maps it onto a DRB; the new QoS flow with explicit RRC signalling procedure (A.3), which has the identical "gNB receives a downlink packet with a new QFI from UPF" step before reconfiguring the DRB mapping via RRC; and the UE-initiated uplink QoS flow procedure (A.6), where the gNB forwards uplink packets to the UPF including the corresponding QFI.

question: In mission-critical interworking with a Land Mobile Radio system, which procedures put the IWF and the LMR user in the same step?
reference_answer: Three procedures in TS 23.283 have a step where the IWF and the LMR user directly interact: (1) clause 10.13.3.2 'Group call with talker ID update initiated by an LMR user on an interworking group defined in the LMR system', where the IWF receives knowledge of the LMR user's talker ID and updates the MCPTT server accordingly; (2) clause 10.5.10 'Floor control in private call controlled by the MCPTT system', where the floor is granted to the LMR user via the IWF, and voice media flows from the LMR user via the IWF to the MCPTT server; (3) clause 10.5.9 'Floor control in private call controlled by the LMR system', where media flows from the LMR user to the IWF, and the IWF indicates that the floor has been taken by or is idle for the LMR user. In all three, the IWF is the node that directly carries the LMR user's floor/media state into the MCPTT system.

question: In FLUS/NBMP live-uplink-streaming call flows, which procedures put the EA (Enabling Application) and the UA (UE Application) in the same step?
reference_answer: Three call-flow mappings in TS 26.939 clause 8.4 have a step where the UA and the EA directly interact: (1) clause 8.4.2.4.1, where the UE Application (UA) makes a request through F8 to the Enabling Application (EA) to start a live session, and the EA later responds to the UA with Control Sink and Media Sink information; (2) clause 8.4.3.4.1, with the same UA-to-EA live-session request and the EA responding to the UA with FLUS Control Sink and Media Sink information after MPE capability discovery; (3) clause 8.4.4.3 'Interfaces', again showing the UA making the F8 request to the EA to start a live session and the EA responding to the UA with the FLUS Sink information. In all three, F8 is the interface over which the UA and EA exchange these session-start/response messages.

question: Which procedures put the ME and the USIM in the same step, i.e. where the ME and the USIM directly exchange information for false-base-station protection?
reference_answer: Three procedures in TS 33.809 clause 6.9.2 have a step where the ME and the USIM directly interact: (1) clause 6.9.2.2.1 'Protection Key Agreement (PKA) and Protection Key Transfer (PKT) procedure', where the ME sends the NONCE to the USIM to initiate key derivation and the USIM returns an indication to the ME once CKp has been generated; (2) clause 6.9.2.3.1 'Security procedure for broadcast messages', where the ME sends the EKRBS and <bsGKI,bsGNI> (and HASHMS or the concatenated DL_ARFCN+message) to the USIM, and the USIM decrypts EKRBS, computes XMAC-I and returns it to the ME for comparison against MAC-I; (3) clause 6.9.2.3.2 'Security procedure for unicast messages', where the ME again sends EKRBS, <bsGKI,bsGNI>, sensitive information and NONCE to the USIM, and the USIM derives Ke and returns it to the ME so the ME can generate the keystream and encrypt the sensitive information.

question: Which procedures put the ECS and the EES in the same step?
reference_answer: Five procedures directly involve the EES sending a request to the ECS (or the ECS acting on it) in the same step: (1) EES registration (TS 23.558 clause 8.4.4.2.2) - the EES sends an EES registration request to the ECS, which verifies credentials and responds; (2) EES registration update (8.4.4.2.3) - the EES sends an update request, the ECS updates the stored registration; (3) EES de-registration (8.4.4.2.4) - the EES sends a de-registration request, the ECS removes the registration; (4) the client-driven 5GMS Edge Processing management procedure (TS 26.501 clause 8.1), whose 'EES Registration with ECS' step has the EES register directly with the ECS that is in authority over the target EDN; (5) the EES registering to ECS using the Eecs_EESRegistration_Request operation (TS 29.558 clause 6.2.2.2.2), where the ECS verifies the EES identity/authorization and creates the registration resource.

question: Which procedures put the LMF and the NRF in the same step?
reference_answer: Two positioning procedures put the LMF and the NRF in the same step for discovering other LMFs: (1) Positioning of a target UE (TS 23.273 clause 6.17.4) - the serving LMF may invoke an Nnrf_NFDiscovery Request to an NRF, including a PRU indication and area, and the NRF selects other PRU-serving LMFs and returns their profiles to the serving LMF in an Nnrf_NFDiscovery Response; (2) PRU Utilization (TS 23.700-71 clause 6.16.3.2) - if the LMF needs PRU information it invokes an Nnrf_NFDiscovery Request to the NRF (including NF type=LMF, cell ID/list, PRU indication), and the NRF returns a response with LMF ID and PRU information.

question: I need every place where the AC and the EEC are involved in the same step of a procedure.
reference_answer: Seven edge-enabler procedures put the Application Client (AC) and the Edge Enabler Client (EEC) directly in the same step, each following an AC-sends-request / EEC-validates-and-responds pattern: (1) ACR trigger request (TS 23.558 clause 8.14.2.4) - the AC sends an ACR trigger request, the EEC validates credentials and responds; (2) EEC services subscription (8.14.2.5.2) - the AC sends a subscription request, the EEC creates the subscription and responds; (3) EEC services subscription update (8.14.2.5.4) - same pattern for updates; (4) AC registration (8.14.2.2.2) - the AC sends an AC registration request, the EEC registers it and responds; (5) ACR request (TS 23.700-98 clause 7.34.2.2.4) - equivalent ACR request/response between AC and EEC; (6) AC subscription request (7.34.2.2.5) - equivalent subscription request/response; (7) AC registration request (7.34.2.2.2) - equivalent registration request/response. In all seven, the EEC checks the AC's security credentials before acting.

question: Which procedures put the AAA server and the HSS in the same step?
reference_answer: Two procedures have a step where the AAA server and the HSS act together. In TS 29.273 Annex E.2 (Successful call flow, untrusted non-3GPP access via ePDG), the 3GPP AAA Server retrieves authentication vectors for the UE directly from the HSS, and later downloads the user's subscription information from the HSS after successful authentication. In TS 43.902 clause 5.1.1.3.7 (EGAN Registration and subscriber management in PS Domain, HSS purge procedure), the HSS initiates termination of a registration by sending a Registration-Termination-Request to the AAA server, which deletes the subscriber information and answers with a Registration-Termination-Answer.

question: For PIN element registration and management, which procedures put the PEMC and the PIN server in the same step?
reference_answer: Two procedures have a step where the PEMC and the PIN server act together. In TS 23.542 clause 8.5.8.2.1 (PIN client requests to join into a PIN), after a new PIN client joins, the PEMC sends a PIN status notify message to the PIN server containing the details of the new PIN client (including PIN client ID and GPSI). In TS 23.700-78 clause 7.13.2.2 (Procedures of PEMC registration), the PEMC sends a Registration Request (including GPSI) to the PIN server, and the PIN server checks the PEMC's subscription and role with the 5GS before responding to the PEMC with an allocated PEMC ID or a failure cause.

question: In network slice communication service management, which procedures put the EGMF and the NSCE server in the same step?
reference_answer: Two procedures have a step where the NSCE server invokes network-slice management services exposed by the EGMF. In TS 23.435 clause 9.12.2.1.2 (Slice related Communication Service Reconfiguration), after receiving a reconfiguration request from the VAL server, the NSCE server initiates the Slice Service update procedure by using the network slice modification management service exposed by the EGMF (as defined in TS 28.531 by SA5). In TS 23.700-99 clause 6.19.1.2 (Slice requirements alignment capability), when the NSCE server decides the slice requirements need updating, it performs the network slice modification operation by using the modifyMOIAttributes operation of the management service exposed by the EGMF.

question: Where do the WLAN and the WT (WLAN Termination) act together in the same step of a procedure?
reference_answer: In TS 36.300 LTE-WLAN Aggregation (LWA), the WT and WLAN resources appear together in the same step in both the WT Addition procedure (clause 22A.1.7.1) and the WT Release procedure (clause 22A.1.7.3). In WT Addition, the eNB sends the WT Addition Request message asking the WT to allocate WLAN resources for specific E-RABs, and the WT responds whether it can admit the full or partial WLAN resource request. In WT Release, the WT sends the WT Release Required message to the eNB, and the WT then initiates the release of all allocated WLAN resources.

question: In UAV detect-and-avoid support, which procedures place the UAE (server/client) and the UAS application specific server in the same step, exchanging DAA support information?
reference_answer: TS 23.700-98/700-55 clause 7.6.2.4 has two DAA (Detect-And-Avoid) support procedures where the UAE and the UAS application specific server exchange DAA information in the same step: the client-initiated DAA support procedure (7.6.2.4.1), where the UAE server sends the DAA support information to the UAS application specific server after recording the DAA event and client location; and the server-initiated DAA support procedure (7.6.2.4.2), where the UAS application specific server sends DAA support information (e.g. other UAVs in proximity) to the UAE server, which the UAE server verifies and forwards to the UAE client.

question: For an MCPTT user initiating a private call to an LMR party, which procedures place the LMR party, the MCPTT client/server and the SDP offer in the same step?
reference_answer: TS 23.283 clause 10.4 has two MCPTT-to-LMR private call setup procedures where the MCPTT client, the called LMR party and the SDP offer appear in the same initiating step: automatic commencement mode (10.4.2.1) and manual commencement mode (10.4.3.1). In both, the MCPTT client sends an MCPTT private call request toward the MCPTT server containing the MCPTT IDs for the calling MCPTT party and the called LMR party plus an SDP offer with one or more media types, which the MCPTT server then forwards toward the IWF for the LMR interworking.

question: For rendering AR media in an IMS communication session, which procedures put the AR device and the RTP channel in the same step?
reference_answer: Two AR-media-rendering procedures in TS 23.700-87 put the AR device and the RTP channel together in one step: the general 'Network rendering process' (clause 6.9.2), where IMS sends the rendered AR media to the calling/called user's AR device over the normal audio/video RTP channel, and the detailed 'Terminal Rendering Process' (clause 6.9.2.1), where UE-A (the AR device) sends its rendered AR audio/video media to the peer through the RTP channel.

question: Which procedures put the CS domain and GERAN in the same step?
reference_answer: Two CS Fallback procedures in TS 23.272 put the CS domain and GERAN together in the same step: 'Mobile Originating call in Active Mode - No PS HO support' (clause 6.3), where the eNodeB can trigger RRC connection release with redirection to GERAN or UTRAN for the CS Fallback call, and 'Mobile Originated or Mobile terminated call rejected by the MME' (clause 6.6), where a Service Reject with a reason code results in the UE selecting GERAN or UTRAN CS Domain.

question: Which procedures involve the PLR and the UPF in the same step?
reference_answer: Two PMFP packet-loss-rate measurement procedures in TS 24.193 put the PLR measurement and the UPF together across their steps: the UE-initiated PLR measurement (clause 5.4.6.1), where the UE sends PMFP PLR count/report request messages to the UPF and the UPF counts and reports UL packets, and the network-initiated PLR measurement (clause 5.4.7.1), where the UPF sends the PMFP PLR count/report request messages to the UE for DL packets.

question: For ProSe direct discovery, which procedures put the HPLMN and WLAN in the same step?
reference_answer: Two ProSe direct discovery procedures in TS 23.303 put the ProSe Function in HPLMN and WLAN together in the same step: the restricted-discovery 'Announce Request (non-roaming)' procedure (clause 5.3.3.2A), where the UE announces using radio resources authorised by E-UTRAN or WLAN and, for 'on demand' announcing, waits on the ProSe Function in HPLMN, and the open-discovery 'Monitor request (roaming)' procedure (clause 5.3.3.5), where a UE intending to use WLAN-based PC5 for monitoring establishes a secure connection with the ProSe Function in HPLMN.

question: Which procedures put the ADRF and ML models in the same step?
reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 23.288 clause 6.2B put the ADRF and ML Model handling in the same step: (1) "ML Model Storage in ADRF" (6.2B.5), where the NWDAF containing MTLF requests the ADRF to store or update an ML Model via Nadrf_MLModelManagement_StorageRequest, and the ADRF stores/downloads and acknowledges; (2) "ML Model removal from ADRF" (6.2B.6), where the NWDAF containing MTLF requests the ADRF to delete a previously stored ML Model via Nadrf_MLModelManagement_Delete, and the ADRF deletes it and returns the result.

question: Which procedures put the PDUID and the RPAUID in the same step?
reference_answer: Two restricted ProSe discovery "Announce Request" procedures in TS 23.303 clause 5.3.3 have the same preparatory step (step 0) linking PDUID and RPAUID: the application client in the UE retrieves the PDUID and provides it to the ProSe Application Server, which allocates an RPAUID for that PDUID, stores the PDUID-RPAUID binding, and returns the RPAUID to the UE. This appears identically in (1) the non-roaming Announce Request (5.3.3.2A) and (2) the roaming/inter-PLMN Announce Request (5.3.3.3A).

question: Which procedures put the GMSCA, the MSRN and VMSCB in the same step?
reference_answer: Two number-portability call-routing procedures in TS 23.066 contain the identical step "GMSCA uses the MSRN to route the call to VMSCB": (1) "International SOR for a Non-ported Number" (B.4.5), where HLRB returns an SRI ack with an MSRN to GMSCA which then routes to VMSCB; (2) "Call to a Ported Number - Direct Routeing" (C.3.2), where HLRA returns the MSRN to GMSCA, which again routes the call to VMSCB.

question: Which procedures put the GMLC and the LRF in the same step?
reference_answer: Two location-continuity handover procedures in TS 23.271 clause 9.4.5.4 have the LRF and a GMLC acting together in the same step: (1) "Location Continuity for E-UTRAN Handover to WLAN" (9.4.5.4.3), where during the emergency call an LRF is assigned and a source location server (e.g. a GMLC) is chosen; (2) "Location Continuity for WLAN Handover to E-UTRAN, UTRAN or GERAN" (9.4.5.4.4), where after handover the LRF may instigate an MT-LR request via the target GMLC if needed.

question: For DRBs with UP integrity protection, which procedures put the DRB and UP integrity handling in the same step?
reference_answer: Two security procedures in TS 33.401 have a step that both configures/activates UP integrity protection and applies it per DRB: (1) the "UP integrity protection activation mechanism" (7.3.4), where the eNB indicates in the RRC Connection Reconfiguration message which DRBs have UP integrity protection activated, and both the eNB and the UE generate KUPint and start UP integrity protection for those DRBs; (2) the dual-connectivity "Activation of encryption/decryption" procedure (E.2.3), where the SeNB shall activate UP integrity protection per DRB according to the received UP integrity protection policy and indicate that to the UE.

question: For PS to CS access transfer with media anchoring, which procedures put the ATCF and the ATGW in the same step?
reference_answer: Two SRVCC signalling flows in TS 24.237 Annex A have the ATCF configuring the ATGW in the same step: (1) "PS to CS Access Transfer with ATCF and media anchored" (A.18.3), where, on receiving the access transfer message, the ATCF correlates the session using the C-MSISDN and updates the ATGW by sending it a Configure ATGW message (acknowledged by the ATGW); (2) "Session origination with PS to CS SRVCC enhancements" (A.4.2), where the ATCF reserves resources in and configures the ATGW as part of establishing the original session.

question: Which procedures put SL positioning and the SLPKMF in the same step?
reference_answer: Two sidelink (SL) positioning security solutions in TS 33.893 have the UE contacting the SLPKMF for SL positioning key material in the same step: (1) the group-based "Security flows" solution (6.15.2.1), where the UE establishes a secure connection with the Sidelink Positioning Key Management Function (SLPKMF) and sends it a Key Request including the Ranging/SL positioning application identifier; (2) the broadcast "Solution details" (6.28.2), where UE1 sends a broadcast authorization request to the SL Positioning Key Management Function (SLPKMF) including its UE ID and Zone ID for the SL Ranging/positioning action.

question: In NR-NR and E-UTRA-NR dual connectivity mobility, which procedures put the MN and the SN in the same step?
reference_answer: Five dual-connectivity mobility procedures in TS 37.340 clause 10 have steps where the MN and the SN act directly with each other: (1) clause 10.17.1 'MR-DC with 5GC' (RRC_INACTIVE resume with UE Context Retrieve) - the target MN sends an SN Addition Request to the SN, which replies with an SN Addition Request Acknowledge, and the source MN later sends an SN Release Request to the SN; (2) clause 10.3.1 'EN-DC' (SN-initiated SN Modification) - the SN sends the SgNB Modification Required to the MN, which forwards the SN RRC reconfiguration to the UE and back; (3) clause 10.3.2 'MR-DC with 5GC' (SN-initiated SN Modification with LTM) - the SN sends the SN Modification Required to the MN, and the MN provides data forwarding address information to the SN; (4) clause 10.4.1 'EN-DC' (SN-initiated SN Release) - the SN sends the SgNB Release Required, and the MN provides data forwarding addresses to the SN in the SgNB Release Confirm; (5) clause 10.9.1 'EN-DC' (inter-eNB handover to SgNB addition) - the target MN sends an SgNB Addition Request to the target SN, which replies with an SgNB Addition Request Acknowledge and provides forwarding addresses.

question: I need every place where the NWDAF and the UPF are involved in the same step of a procedure.
reference_answer: Three procedures put the NWDAF and the UPF in the same step. TS 23.288 6.16.4 (PFD Determination analytics procedure): the NWDAF collects User Data Usage Measures from the UPF via SMF, and the UPF may also report data directly to the NWDAF. TS 23.700-62 6.7.3.1 (Subscription to UPF for Data Collection for "Any UE"): the UPF registers its profile in NRF, the NWDAF sends Nupf_EventExposure Subscribe to the relevant UPF(s), and the UPF sends Nupf_EventExposure Notify back to the NWDAF. TS 23.700-62 6.9.3.1 (UPF data collection for single UE): the NWDAF determines the event ID for UPF event exposure, the UPF registers to SMF with supported event exposure, and the UPF sends notifications toward the NWDAF (directly or via SMF).

question: Which procedures put the W-AGF and the AMF in the same step?
reference_answer: Three procedures put the W-AGF and the AMF in the same step. TS 23.316 7.2.8.2 (AUN3 device De-registration via W-5GAN): the AMF sends an N2 UE Context Release Command to the W-AGF, and the W-AGF removes the context and confirms with an N2 UE Context Release Complete back to the AMF. TS 23.316 7.3.2 (5G-RG or Network Requested PDU Session Modification via W-5GAN): the AMF sends an N2 PDU Session Resource Modify Request to the W-AGF, and the W-AGF acknowledges with an N2 PDU Session Resource Modify Response, also forwarding NAS messages between the 5G-RG and AMF. TS 33.887 6.9.2.1 (AUN3 device authentication procedure): the AMF derives the WAGF key and sends it to the W-AGF via NAS Security Mode Command, after which the W-AGF/RG derive further keys.

question: Which procedures put the MME and the SGSN in the same step?
reference_answer: Three execution-phase procedures in TS 23.401 clause 5.5.2 (inter-RAT handover) put the MME and the SGSN in the same step, all around the Forward Relocation Complete exchange. (1) Clause 5.5.2.2.3 (UTRAN Iu mode to E-UTRAN handover, execution phase): once the UE has arrived at the target side, the target MME informs the source SGSN by sending the Forward Relocation Complete Notification message, and the source SGSN acknowledges; later the source SGSN releases resources towards the source RNC and, if a Serving GW change was indicated, deletes EPS bearer resources. (2) Clause 5.5.2.4.3 (GERAN A/Gb mode to E-UTRAN handover, execution phase): the same Forward Relocation Complete Notification/acknowledge exchange occurs between the target MME and source SGSN, after which the source SGSN stops data forwarding and cleans up resources towards the source BSS. (3) Annex D.3.8.3 (execution phase for a Gn/Gp SGSN interworking case): the target MME informs the old SGSN via a Forward Relocation Complete message, the old SGSN acknowledges and stops data forwarding.

question: Which procedures put the IWF and the MME in the same step?
reference_answer: Three MAP-D interworking procedures in TS 29.305 Annex A.4.4 put the IWF and the MME in the same step, all involving the IWF relaying HSS-originated MAP messages to the MME. (1) Clause A.4.4.5.2 ("Insert Subscriber Data over MAP D"): if the received MAP InsertSubscriberData contains SMS-related data, the IWF maps it into an IDR sent towards the MME, and later receives the corresponding IDA from the MME. (2) Clause A.4.4.6.2 ("Delete Subscriber Data over MAP D"): the IWF maps SMS-related DeleteSubscriberData into a DSR towards the MME and receives a DSA from the MME; if the SMS subscription is withdrawn, the IWF also sends an IDR to the MME to remove the MME's SMS registration. (3) Clause A.4.4.7 ("Reset"): the IWF exchanges Reset (RSR/RSA) messages with the MME, receiving an RSA from the MME and sending an RSR unchanged to the MME.

question: For an AF provisioning expected-UE-behaviour parameters, which procedures put the AF and the UDM in the same step?
reference_answer: Two procedures put the AF and the UDM together acting in the same step: the NEF service operations information flow for external parameter provisioning in TS 23.502 clause 4.15.6.2, where the UDM authorises the AF-provisioned parameters, resolves the GPSI to SUPI, and requests to create/update/delete the data (with subsequent Nudm_ParameterProvision response to the AF/NEF); and the Network Triggered capability indication procedure in TS 23.700-41 clause 6.6.3.1.2, where during UE registration the UDM may interact directly with the SoR AF to provide SoR information to the UE.

question: Which procedures put the CCA, the NRF and the SCP in the same step?
reference_answer: Two procedures put the SCP, the NRF and the CCA together acting in the same step: the Authorization for indirect communication with delegated discovery procedure in TS 33.501 clause 13.4.1.3.2, where the SCP sends an Nnrf_AccessToken_Get access token request to the NRF that may include the NF Service Consumer's CCA received earlier; and the Request of access token on behalf of the consumer procedure in TS 33.875 clause 6.3.2.1, where the SCP sends an access token request to the NRF including the CCA received from the consumer.

question: For edge application discovery via the ECS, which procedures put the ECS and the ECS-ER in the same step?
reference_answer: Two ECS discovery-subscription procedures in TS 23.558 put the ECS and the ECS Enabler Registry (ECS-ER) together in the same step: clause 8.17.2.3.3.2 'Subscribe', where the ECS sends an ECS discovery subscription request to the ECS-ER, and the ECS-ER authorizes it, stores the subscription and sends back a subscription response; and clause 8.17.2.3.3.4 'Subscription update', where the ECS sends an update request to the ECS-ER, which authorizes and updates the stored subscription and returns an update response.

question: Which procedures put the UP data path and the UPF in the same step?
reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 23.700-60, both titled 'Procedures': (1) clause 6.20.3, where after a PDU Session is established, the UPF receives UP data from the application server, which may include PDU Set assistance metadata; (2) clause 6.60.3, where the same UPF-receives-UP-data-from-the-application-server step occurs as the basis for the UPF determining data burst termination (End of Data Burst Indication).

question: Which procedures put the OCS, the PCRF and a Diameter SLA command (with its AVP) in the same step?
reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 29.213: (1) clause 4.7.1 'Initial Spending Limit Report Request' - the OCS sends a Diameter SLA command to the PCRF, carrying a Policy-Counter-Status-Report AVP for each requested policy counter identifier plus a Result-Code AVP; (2) clause 4.7.2 'Intermediate Spending Limit Report Request' - the OCS again sends the Diameter SLA command to the PCRF with Policy-Counter-Status-Report AVP(s) after the PCRF requests an updated list of policy counters.

question: Which procedures put the NRF and a UUID in the same step?
reference_answer: Both NRF registration procedures in TS 29.510 clause 5.2.2.2 put the NRF and a UUID in the same step: NF (other than NRF) registration to NRF (5.2.2.2.2), where the NF Service Consumer's PUT request identifies the NF Instance by a UUID version 4 nfInstanceId, and if that UUID is sent with upper-case hex digits the NRF must still handle it as lower-case; and Shared Data registration to NRF (5.2.2.2.4), where the same UUID-formatting rule applies to the sharedDataId used in the PUT request the NRF processes.

question: Which procedures put the AMF and the NEF in the same step?
reference_answer: The AMF and the NEF appear together in a step across six procedures: the AMF service operations information flow (TS 23.502, 4.15.3.2.1), where the AMF sends event reports to a subscribing NEF via Namf_EventExposure_Notify; NEF Anchored Mobile Terminated Data Transport (TS 23.502, 4.25.5), where the AMF indicates UE reachability to the NEF; local-service event subscription in TS 23.700-08 clause 6.15.3, where the NEF subscribes to the AMF for Local Service Subscription events; group event exposure in TS 23.700-74 clause 6.14.3, where the AMF sends event reports to the NEF; and the AmfRegistration information retrieval procedures in TS 29.503 clauses 5.3.2.5.2 and 5.3.2.5.3, where the NEF (as NF service consumer) queries the AMF's 3GPP and non-3GPP registration resources.

question: Which procedures show the NWDAF and the SMF acting in the same step?
reference_answer: The NWDAF and SMF act together in a step across five procedures: session-management congestion-control-experience analytics (TS 23.288, 6.12.4), where the SMF requests or subscribes to NWDAF analytics and also supplies collected data to the NWDAF; UPF data collection for a single UE (TS 23.700-62, 6.9.3.1), where the NWDAF subscribes to the SMF for UPF event exposure and the SMF relays the subscription to the UPF; AF subscription for 5GC information/analytics (TS 23.700-80, 6.8.3.1), where the SMF subscribes to NWDAF analytics for the PDU session after the PCF instructs it to; service-experience analytics collection in TS 23.700-81 clause 6.49.2, where the NWDAF collects service data from SMF/UPF; and the SmfRegistration information retrieval procedure (TS 29.503, 5.3.2.5.7), where the NWDAF, as NF service consumer, queries the SMF registration resource.

question: For NWDAF analytics that depend on operations-and-maintenance data, which procedures put the NWDAF and OAM in the same step?
reference_answer: The NWDAF and OAM appear together in a step across six procedures: prepared-analytics-subscription transfer (TS 23.288, 6.1B.2.3), where the source and target NWDAFs collect data from NFs or OAM; the QoS-sustainability procedure for a coarse-granularity area (TS 23.288, 6.9.4.1), where the NWDAF collects data from the OAM; the estimated-QoS information-exposure procedure (TS 23.700-60, 6.45.3), where the NWDAF subscribes to OAM services; service-experience analytics in TS 23.700-81 clause 6.18.3, where the NWDAF again collects data from the OAM; and security log collection via NF EventExposure APIs (TS 33.738, 6.6.2.2) and via OAM (TS 33.738, 6.6.2.3), where the OAM (or an operator's AF) requests NF anomalous-behaviour analytics from the NWDAF, and the NWDAF derives analytics or retrieves security logs using OAM- and NRF-supplied inputs.

question: For multicast/broadcast MBS sessions, which procedures put the MBS session and the SMF in the same step?
reference_answer: The MBS session and the SMF act together in a step across three procedures: multicast session leave requested by the network or MBS session release (TS 23.247, 7.2.2.3), where the SMF removes UEs from the MBS session and informs the AMF/NG-RAN via N1N2MessageTransfer; selecting an alternative AMF for a Broadcast MBS session at AMF failure (TS 23.527, 8.3.2.4), where the MB-SMF sends Namf_MBSBroadcast_ContextUpdate and receives the ContextStatusNotify confirming the new controlling AMF; and broadcast session establishment (TS 23.700-47, 6.13.3.2), where the MB-SMF continues the MBS Session Creation procedure defined in TS 23.247.

question: We are tracing charging-and-policy control across access types — which procedures put PCC rules and the PCRF in the same step?
reference_answer: PCC rules and the PCRF appear together in a step across six procedures: network recovery on PDP context/bearer update (TS 23.380, 5.1.2) and network recovery informing the UE at P-CSCF failure (TS 23.380, 5.2.2), both where the PCRF provides PCC rules in a CCA; UE-initiated resource request/release on S2a (TS 23.402, 6.7.1), where the PCRF makes a PCC decision and updates PCC rules at the PDN GW via the Policy and Charging Rules Provision Procedure; enabling of IP flows (TS 29.213, B.3.2), where the PCRF updates the flow status of PCC rules to open the gates; IP-CAN session establishment for NSWO traffic (TS 29.213, E.4.2.2), where the H-PCRF provisions PCC rules to the V-PCRF/BPCF, which stores and enforces them; and BPCF-initiated IP-CAN session modification (TS 29.213, E.4.4.2.2), where the BPCF reports a PCC rule failure to the (V-/H-)PCRF via Diameter CCR.

question: For Isolated E-UTRAN Operation for Public Safety, which procedures put IOPS, the MC connectivity function, and MCPTT clients in the same step?
reference_answer: IOPS, the IOPS MC connectivity function and MCPTT clients act together in a step across seven procedures in TS 23.180: IOPS group call (10.5.1.3) and IOPS emergency group call (10.5.1.4), where the connectivity function distributes group-call announcements/responses among IOPS MCPTT clients; IOPS private call setup (10.5.2.3), emergency private call setup (10.5.2.6), and private call release (10.5.2.5), where the connectivity function relays call setup/ringing/release requests and responses between MCPTT client 1 and client 2 by IP address; a further private-call ringing variant (10.5.2.4); and IOPS floor control (10.5.3.3), where the connectivity function distributes floor-request and floor-taken messages to the target IOPS MCPTT group.

question: I need every place where the AF, a GPSI, and the NEF's NIDD configuration are involved in the same step.
reference_answer: The AF, GPSI, and NIDD configuration act together in a step across three clauses of TS 23.502: NIDD configuration establishment (4.25.3), where the AF sends Nnef_NIDDConfiguration_Create identifying the UE by GPSI, the NEF authorises it with the UDM via Nudm_NIDDAuthorisation_Get, and returns a TLTRI to the AF; NEF-anchored MT data delivery (4.25.5), where the NEF looks up the 5GS QoS Flow context by GPSI before accepting an AF's Nnef_NIDD_Delivery request; and NIDD authorization update notification (4.25.6), where the NEF informs the AF of a change in a GPSI-identified user's NIDD authorization status.

question: For positioning reference-unit subscription and registration, which procedures put the AMF, PRU handling, and the UDM in the same step?
reference_answer: The AMF and the UDM cooperate over PRU handling in the same step across two clauses of TS 23.700-71: clause 6.15.3.2, where the AMF updates PRU state information at the UDM and separately invokes Nudm_SDM_Get to obtain and check PRU privacy settings; and clause 6.16.3.1, where the AMF invokes Nudm_SDM_Get to verify the UE's subscription data includes PRU subscription, rejecting Registration if it does not.

question: For network-slice capability exposure toward vertical (VAL) applications, which procedures put the NEF, OAM, SEAL, and the VAL server in the same step?
reference_answer: The NEF, OAM, SEAL, and the VAL server act together in a step across two clauses of TS 23.700-99: clause 6.3.1.2, where the network slice capability enablement server maps a VAL application's requirement to a slice API backed by a list of NEF APIs, SEAL APIs, or OAM-provided APIs; and clause 6.3.1.3, where the VAL server sends a slice API invocation request to that enablement server, referencing the same NEF/SEAL/OAM-backed service APIs.

question: For ported-number call routing with routeing-number insertion, which procedures put GMSCA, the IAM message, and the MSISDN/RN together in the same step?
reference_answer: GMSCA, the IAM message, and the MSISDN/RN act together in a step across three clauses of TS 23.066 (C.3.3, C.3.4, C.3.5): each shows GMSCA using the RN (plus MSISDN) to route the call to GMSCB in the subscription network, with the RN optionally added to the IAM message depending on the interconnect agreement.

question: For VAL applications discovering and subscribing to SEALDD service, which procedures put CAPIF, SEALDD service, and the VAL server together in the same step?
reference_answer: CAPIF, SEALDD service, and the VAL server act together in a step across eight clauses spanning TS 23.433 (9.2.2.2, 9.3.2.1, 9.7.2.1, 9.8.2, 9.9.2.1) and TS 23.700-34 (6.2.2.2, 6.12.2.2, 6.18.2.2): the VAL server discovers a SEALDD server via CAPIF, then sends a service request such as Sdd_RegularTransmission, Sdd_URLLCTransmission, a transmission-quality-measurement subscription, a bandwidth-limit request, or a SEALDD service subscription request; the SEALDD server performs authorization and responds accordingly.

question: Which procedures put MBMS coverage, the MCCH, and the session's TMGI in the same step?
reference_answer: MBMS coverage, the MCCH, and the session TMGI appear together in a step across two near-identical clauses of TS 23.468 (5.3.3.2 and 5.3.3.3): the UE monitors the SIBs to detect the TMGI advertised on MCCH, which is how it determines it has returned to MBMS coverage for the MBMS bearer service.

question: For IoT traffic-pattern coordination, which procedures put the IoT-PCS server, SEAL-based signalling, and the IoT-App VAL server together in the same step?
reference_answer: The IoT-PCS server and the IoT-App VAL/SEAL server act together in a step across two clauses of TS 23.700-97: clause 5.7.2.2, where the IoT-PCS server aggregates traffic-pattern and monitoring subscriptions from multiple IoT-App VAL/SEAL servers, sends traffic-pattern update notifications to them, and executes management/5GC-exposure procedures on their behalf; and clause 5.7.2.4, where the IoT-PCS server requests service-specific traffic-pattern configuration for given UEs from the IoT-App VAL/SEAL server.

question: For 5G ProSe relay key derivation, which procedures put the PRUK identity, the Relay Service Code (RSC), and the SUCI together in the same step?
reference_answer: The PRUK identity, the RSC, and the SUCI act together in a step across three clauses of TS 33.740: emergency UE-to-network relay connection (6.27.2), where a USIM-equipped Remote UE sends a Direct Communication Request containing PRUK ID or SUCI, Emergency RSC, and a key-freshness parameter to the Relay, which then runs UP/CP security procedures; UE-to-UE relay key request (6.3.2.1), where the Source UE sends a DCR with PRUK ID/SUCI and the Relay's RSC, and the Relay forwards a Key Request with the same identifiers to the 5GC; and UE-to-UE relay-2 authorization (6.31.2.1), where relay-2 sends a further Key Request with the Source UE's PRUK ID/SUCI and the previously received RSC to the 5GC to derive KNRP and complete security-mode signalling.

question: For GAN security-gateway resolution, which procedures put a DNS query, the SEGW's FQDN, and the security gateway together in the same step?
reference_answer: A DNS query, the SEGW's FQDN, and the SEGW act together in a step across two clauses (TS 43.318, 8.4.1.6.1; TS 43.902, 5.2.5.4.1): if the MS was provided the FQDN of the Default or Serving SEGW, the MS performs a DNS query via the generic IP access network interface to resolve it to an IP address, unless it already has a provisioned IP address for the SEGW.

question: For application-client-managed application context relocation, which procedures put the AC, ACR handling, EDGE-interface signalling, and the EEC together in the same step?
reference_answer: The AC, ACR handling, and the EEC act together over EDGE interfaces in a step across four clauses: EEC-services subscription (TS 23.558, 8.14.2.5.2) and the equivalent AC subscription request (TS 23.700-98, 7.34.2.2.5), where the AC subscribes the EEC to EAS discovery/dynamic-information and ACR-management operations (ACR notifications, ACR monitoring, or EEC-managed ACR) over EDGE-1; and ACR-modification notification (TS 23.700-98, 7.6.2.1.1 and 7.6.2.1.2), where the EEC detects a change in expected UE behaviour reported by the AC over EDGE-5 and optionally notifies the AC back of the ACR modification result.

question: For emergency IMS registration under RLOS, which procedures put the CSCF and RLOS handling together in the same step?
reference_answer: The CSCF and RLOS handling act together in a step across two clauses of TS 23.228: clause Z.3.1, where the P-CSCF, based on the RLOS indication for a roaming subscriber without a roaming agreement, forwards the Register information to the S-CSCF configured for RLOS, and the S-CSCF either responds 420 (GIBA supported) or 403 with a temporary unauthenticated registration record; and clause Z.3.2.1, the I-CSCF variant, where the P-CSCF forwards Register information to the I-CSCF, which queries the HSS and selects an RLOS-capable S-CSCF, and the S-CSCF likewise creates a temporary registration record on failed authentication.

question: For CS-domain call teardown at IMS/PSTN boundaries, which procedures put the MSC and a REL message together in the same step?
reference_answer: The MSC and a REL message act together in a step across two clauses: call-waiting/setup signalling (TS 23.292, 7.6.3.10.1), where the MSC Server may send a REL response immediately depending on call-waiting settings, and maps a Release Complete to a REL message; and video-call failure handling (TS 23.903, 4.4.1), where MSC B sends a REL message to MSC A in each failure scenario (unsupported video calls, resource unavailability, or callee rejection).

question: For discovering edge configuration servers when OAM-provided information is unavailable, which procedures put the ECS and OAM configuration together in the same step?
reference_answer: The ECS and OAM configuration act together in a step across three clauses: partner-ECS query authorization (TS 23.558, 8.17.2.4.2.2), where the partner ECS authorizes the request and gathers EDN provisioning information; and ECS discovery (TS 23.700-98, 7.50.2.2 and 7.50.2.3), where the Primary ECS retrieves configuration information of partner ECS(s) using preconfigured information, information configured via OAM, or a discovery mechanism via the ECS-ER.

question: For UE-mobility-driven data-collection handover, which procedures put the AMF and the DCCF together in the same step?
reference_answer: The AMF and the DCCF act together in a step across four clauses: source/target DCCF subscription-context transfer on UE mobility (TS 23.288, 6.2.6.3.8), where the source DCCF subscribes to AMF UE-mobility events and determines whether to transfer the subscription context to a target DCCF; the equivalent multi-UE transfer procedure (TS 23.700-81, 6.66.2); area-of-interest notification (TS 23.700-81, 6.12.2), where the AMF notifies DCCF-1 that the UE has entered a new area of interest; and MTLF re-training data collection (TS 23.700-81, 6.6.2), where the NWDAF containing MTLF may collect data from NFs including the AMF/DCCF/ADRF to re-train an ML model.

question: For MCPTT signalling-key distribution and MC service delivery, which procedures put an MC UE and the MCX server together in the same step?
reference_answer: An MC UE and the MCX server act together in a step across four clauses: eMBMS-bearer-based MC service delivery decision (TS 23.783, 6.32.1.1), where the MC service server analyses location information and may announce an eMBMS bearer; signalling-key download (TS 33.180, 5.8.2), where the MCX Server sends a key-download message (SIP NOTIFY/MESSAGE) to the MC UE and the MC UE confirms extraction with a 200 OK; and CSK/SPK-protected session signalling across a security gateway (TS 33.180, L.4.2 and L.4.3), where signalling between the client and MCX server is protected with the CSK and between the MCX server and the SeGy with the SPK.

question: For data-channel-signalling-function registration and discovery, which procedures put the DCSF and the NRF together in the same step?
reference_answer: The DCSF and the NRF act together in a step across two clauses of TS 23.700-87: DCSF registration (6.17.2.1), where the DCSF sends Nnrf_NFManagement_NFRegister_Request and the NRF stores/acknowledges its profile; and DCSF discovery (6.17.2.2), where the IMS AS sends Nnrf_NFDiscovery_Request to the NRF, which returns matching DCSF instance(s) for selection.

question: For L2 UE-to-Network relay selection reporting, which procedures put an SD-RSRP measurement together with candidate relay reporting in the same step?
reference_answer: SD-RSRP measurements and candidate-relay reporting act together in a step across two clauses of TS 38.300 (16.12.6.2 and 16.12.6.3): the L2 U2N Remote UE, after measuring/discovering candidate L2 U2N Relay UE(s) and filtering by relay-selection criteria, reports one or more candidates to the source gNB including the Relay UE ID, its serving cell ID, and SD-RSRP as the sidelink measurement quantity.

question: For MCData group short data service, which procedures put the MCData emergency/imminent-peril state (MCPTT-linked) and SDS group data requests together in the same step?
reference_answer: MCData emergency/imminent-peril state and SDS group data requests act together in a step across three clauses of TS 23.282 (7.4.2.5.2, 7.4.2.6.2, 7.4.2.7.2): MCData client 1 sends a group (session) standalone/data request to the MCData server carrying the group ID or target recipients and a conversation identifier, and if initiating an emergency or imminent-peril short data service communication, sets the corresponding indicator and enters (or is already in) the retained MCData emergency state, tied to the MCPTT emergency state, until explicitly cancelled.

question: For Sh/Ud front-end data access, which procedures put the FE (application-specific front-end) and the UDR together in the same step?
reference_answer: The FE and the UDR act together in a step across two clauses of TS 23.335: transparent-data update flow (A.2.3), where the HSS-FE checks AS permissions, fetches service data via Ud Query, updates it via Ud Update with a sequence-number condition, and the UDR stores the new configuration or responds with the requested data; and subscription-to-notification flow (A.3.2), where the FE sends a Subscription Request to the UDR, and the HSS-FE checks permissions and queries the UDR to fetch data needed to process the subscription/notification.

question: For network-assisted-bitrate reporting from a media session handler, which procedures put the Data Collection AF and ANBR-based network-assistance reporting together in the same step?
reference_answer: The Data Collection AF and ANBR-based network-assistance reporting act together in a step across two clauses of TS 26.501: downlink ANBR reporting (4.7.2.1), where the Direct Data Collection Client in the Media Session Handler reports ANBR-based downlink Network Assistance invocations to the Data Collection AF in the 5GMSd AF over reference point R2; and uplink ANBR reporting (4.7.2.2), the equivalent flow for uplink Network Assistance via the 5GMSu AF.

question: If the AMF handling a Broadcast MBS session fails without restarting and no replacement AMF proactively notifies the network, how does the MB-SMF recover?
reference_answer: The MB-SMF detects that the AMF handling the Broadcast MBS session has failed without restart, and since no Namf_MBSBroadcast_ContextStatusNotify Request arrived from any AMF in the same AMF set, the MB-SMF reselects an alternative AMF itself by sending a Namf_MBSBroadcast_ContextUpdate Request. That request indicates the alternative AMF need not trigger any NGAP message to deliver the stored N2 container (MBS Session Setup/Modification Request Transfer) — it just stores it for use if NG-RAN restoration signalling arrives.

question: Network performance in an area has degraded below a monitored threshold. How does the PCF find out, and what does it do about background data transfer policies affected by it?
reference_answer: The (H-)PCF has already subscribed to network performance from the NWDAF and is notified when performance in the area of interest drops below the configured criteria. On notification, the PCF queries the UDR (Nudr_DataRepository_Query on the BdtData resource) for all stored transfer policies, identifies which ones are affected by the degradation, and for each affected policy determines the ASP whose background traffic will be impacted and which originally requested the warning notification.

question: How do NWDAF instances decide which candidates become Client NWDAFs during the Federated Learning preparation phase?
reference_answer: NWDAFs first register into the NRF with their Federated Learning capability; the Server NWDAF discovers potential Client NWDAFs from the NRF based on criteria such as Federated Learning capability and Analytics ID, and then sends an Nnwdaf_MLPreparation_Request to those candidates carrying Interoperability information (what abilities are needed, e.g. shared-model support) and an indication that they should act as Client NWDAF(s); final selection follows a handshake pattern based on availability and capability.

question: A V2X application server wants ongoing HD-map dynamic information about a specific host vehicle. What does it do first, and what does the VAE server do in response?
reference_answer: The V2X application specific server, already registered with VAE server 1 responsible for the host vehicle, sends a subscribe HD-map-dynamic-information request naming the host vehicle's V2X UE ID and an application-defined proximity range. VAE server 1 stores the subscription, sends a subscription response back to the V2X application server, and begins obtaining and tracking the host vehicle's location from the location management server.

question: A PEMC that's behind a PEGC needs to register with the PINMF. How does its registration request actually get there, and how does the network confirm it's allowed to be a PEMC?
reference_answer: The PEMC sends a Message Transfer Request (containing the Registration Request) to the PEGC, which forwards it as a Transfer Message Request (with the PEMC Transport Address) to the PINMF. The PINMF-A then interacts with the UDR, via the UDM or NEF, to check whether the UE identified by the GPSI has subscribed to be a PEMC — the UDR returns the subscribed PIN-related information, including whether the UE is a PEMC and its Trust Member Group ID if one exists, plus any already-registered PINMF Info for that GPSI.

question: An ECS wants to register with its ECS-ER for the first time. What must it already know, what does it send, and how does it keep the registration alive afterward?
reference_answer: The ECS must already know the address (e.g. URI) of the ECS-ER. It sends an ECS registration request carrying its ECS profile and security credentials, optionally a proposed expiration time, a list of partner ECSPs allowed to receive its information, and (for roaming UEs) DNN/S-NSSAI information. The ECS-ER verifies the credentials, stores the registration, and responds with success/failure and an expiration time; to keep the registration alive the ECS must send a registration update request before that expiration time, otherwise the ECS-ER treats it as implicitly deregistered.

question: In the UAE-layer-assisted change of USS, once the UAE server verifies a USS change request from the serving USS, how does it interact with the NEF to affect the user plane path, and what does it then forward to the UAE client?
reference_answer: Per TS 23.255 clause 7.6.2.3, after verifying the USS change request is authorized, the UAE server translates the change into a UP path change and interacts with the NEF as an AF to influence UP path routing (switching to the target DNAI), per the AF-influence-on-traffic-routing functionality of TS 23.502 clause 4.3.6.3, checking whether it can serve the target DNAI mapped to the target USS. The UAE server then forwards the USS change request to the UAE client, including the target USS information and updated Multi-USS policies, and the UAE client initiates communication with the target USS.

question: In the Send Routing Info for SM mapping via the IWF, what message does the IWF forward on to the HSS after receiving the SMS-GMSC's request, and what does it do with the resulting response?
reference_answer: Per TS 29.305 clause A.3.4.1, after the IWF receives a sendRoutingInfoForSM MAP V3 message from the SMS-GMSC, it sends an SRR (Send Routing Info Request) to the HSS (or SMS Router / IP-SM-GW). On receiving the SRA (Send Routing Info Answer) from the HSS, the IWF sends a sendRoutingInfoForSM Ack message back to the SMS-GMSC, and if the SRA contains information elements requiring an informServiceCentre message, the IWF also sends that message to the SMS-GMSC before closing the MAP dialog.

question: During registration via untrusted non-3GPP access with N3IWF relocation, what message does the AMF send to N3IWF-1 to trigger the relocation, and how does N3IWF-2 know to route the resumed registration to the same AMF?
reference_answer: Per TS 23.700-17 clause 6.11.2.1, the AMF sends a N3IWF Relocation Command to N3IWF-1 that contains a Security Mode Control (SMC) Request message plus the address of N3IWF-2 and an AMF identity (e.g. GUAMI or IP address); N3IWF-1 forwards this to the UE. The UE then connects to N3IWF-2 and sends an IKE_AUTH request containing an EAP-Response/5G-NAS packet with the AMF identity received earlier; N3IWF-2 selects the same AMF based on that received AMF identity and forwards the SMC Complete message to the AMF inside a N3IWF Relocation Notify message, letting the AMF associate it with the existing UE context and resume the registration procedure.

question: Which procedures put the SMF and the UPF in the same step when a PDU Session Anchor is added or removed via an intermediate SMF?
reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 23.502 clause 4.3 put the SMF and the UPF together in the same step: clause 4.3.5.5 ('Removal of additional PDU Session Anchor and Branching Point or UL CL'), where the SMF releases PSA1 via N4 and updates the UPF acting as Branching Point/UL CL; and clause 4.23.9.1 ('Addition of PDU Session Anchor and Branching Point or UL CL controlled by I-SMF'), where the I-SMF uses N4 to establish the new PDU Session Anchor 2 on a selected UPF and update the Branching Point/UL CL via N4.

question: Which procedures put the NEF and the AF in the same step for subscribing to or unsubscribing from Member UE selection assistance?
reference_answer: Two TS 23.502 clause 4.15.13 procedures put the NEF and the AF together in the same step for Member UE selection assistance: clause 4.15.13.1 ('Member UE selection assistance subscribe and update procedure'), where the AF subscribes to Member UE selection assistance by invoking a NEF service operation with its Member UE filtering criteria; and clause 4.15.13.7 ('Member UE selection assistance unsubscribe procedure'), where the AF sends Nnef_MemberUESelectionAssistance_unsubscribe (Subscription Correlation ID) and the NEF deletes the subscription(s) and responds with the operation execution result.

question: Which procedures put the GMS and the MC service server in the same step for group regrouping using a preconfigured MC service group?
reference_answer: Four procedures in TS 23.280 clause 10.15.3 put the GMS and the MC service server together in the same step, since the MC service server is subscribed to the group configuration in the GMS and retrieves regroup-group configuration from it: clause 10.15.3.2.1 (preconfigured group regroup formation in a single MC system), clause 10.15.3.3.1 (preconfigured group regroup formation in multiple MC systems), clause 10.15.3.3.4 (preconfigured group regroup rejection in multiple MC systems), and clause 10.15.3.4.1 (adding a newly affiliated user to an in-progress preconfigured group regroup).

question: Which procedures put the IWF and the LMS in the same step for an event-triggered (unsolicited) location notification, or for using that notified location to answer a 'who is talking' query, between an MC system and an LMR system?
reference_answer: Three procedures in TS 23.283 clause 10.11 put the IWF and the LMS (via the MC service server) together in the same step: clause 10.11.4.2.2.1 (event-triggered location notification from the IWF in the LMR system to the LMS in the MC system), clause 10.11.4.2.2.2 (the reverse notification, from the LMS in the MC system to the IWF in the LMR system), and clause 10.11.3 ('Location of current talker'), where the MCPTT server checks the privacy policy of the current talking IWF user and provides that user's location, obtained via the IWF, to the MCPTT clients on the call.

question: Which procedures put the GMS and the IWF in the same step for subscribing to group configuration information between an MC system and its interworking function?
reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 23.283 clause 10.2.3 put the GMS and the IWF together in the same step, in opposite directions of subscription: clause 10.2.3.6 ('IWF subscribes to group configuration'), where the IWF subscribes to group configuration information stored in the group management server (GMS) of the primary MC system; and clause 10.2.3.8 ('MC system subscribes to group configuration'), where the group management server of the MC system instead subscribes to group configuration information stored in the IWF.

question: In the study on further enhancement for network automation, which solutions put the NWDAF, the AMF and the SMF together in the same step?
reference_answer: TR 23.700-81: clause 6.11.2 ("Procedure for providing HPLMN load level analytics to VPLMN") has the V-NWDAF request Network Slice load level analytics from the H-NWDAF upon an AMF subscription/request; clause 6.24.2.2 ("Procedure for usage of Federated Learning in Abnormal Behaviour") has Client NWDAFs collect raw data from the SMF and the AMF respectively to train an Abnormal Classifier.

question: In the study on 5GC architecture enhancements for Time Sensitive Communication, which solutions put the UMIC and the PMIC together in the same step?
reference_answer: TR 23.700-25: clause 6.11.3 ("Procedure for reserve the resource in TSN transport network") has NG-RAN send the uplink/downlink Port Management Information Container (PMIC/UMIC) in the N2 request to carry stream information for the CUC; clause 6.3.3 (timing synchronization resiliency and status reporting) reuses PDU session establishment enhanced for UPF timing resiliency, exposing timing synchronization capability that PMIC/UMIC information relies on.

question: In the study on aligning 5GS support for enabling edge applications, which solutions put the ECSP and the OP (edge operator) together in the same step for edge node sharing?
reference_answer: TR 23.700-98: clause 7.44.2.3 ("EAS discovery for edge node sharing") has ECSP-1 and ECSP-2, under a service-level agreement, let EES-B request the list of registered EASs from partner Operator OP-A's EES-A; clause 7.45.2.2 ("EAS discovery Procedure") has the EES determine the EAS based on the desired ECSP of the UE and the ECSP of the EAS across OP A / OP B; clause 7.45.2.3 ("T-EAS discovery Procedure") has the T-EES determine the T-EAS the same way, using the EEC's home ECSP (identifying its OP).

question: In the study on converging fixed and mobile subscriber data management, which solutions put the UDM and the HSS FE together in the same step?
reference_answer: TR 23.973: clause 6.2.3.1 ("Authentication and Registration") has the UDM interact with the HSS FE to retrieve authentication vectors from the EPS UDR and to relay Update/Cancel Location signalling for single registration; clause 6.2.3.2 ("IP address continuity of interworking without N26 from 5GS to EPS") has the UDM forward Update Location Request/Ack to the HSS FE, which handles it against the EPS UDR and returns the PGW-C+SMF FQDN; clause 6.2.3.3 ("T-ADS for IMS voice") has the UDM forward a T-ADS query to the HSS FE, which queries MME/SGSN and returns T-ADS information back through the UDM; clause 6.2.3.4 ("Supporting IMS related procedures") has the UDM identify IMS Cx/Dx/Sh requests and forward them to the HSS FE, which interacts with the EPS UDR and returns responses via the UDM; clause 6.2.3.6 ("MT SMS domain selection") has the UDM retrieve the SMSF address from the 5GS UDR and forward the MAP Send Routing Info for SM request to the HSS FE to obtain additional MT SMS routing addresses from the EPS side.

question: In the study on satellite backhaul enhancements for non-public networks, which solutions put CAG and the DNN together in the same step for local-service access?
reference_answer: TR 23.700-08: clause 6.23.3 has the UE receive hosting-network selection and access information from the Localized Service Provider, tied to a DNN and CAG-based access; clause 6.32.3 ("Discovery and access local service via PNI-NPN") has the network provide, during Registration, a list of available local services together with the CAG identifiers and validity period for a given DNN-based service.

question: In the study on Ad hoc group communication for MCX services, which solutions put MC (mission critical service) and SDP together in the same step for group call setup?
reference_answer: TR 23.700-76: clause 7.1.3.1.1 ("Ad hoc group communication setup") has an authorized MC service user invite other MC service users into an ad hoc group communication with SDP negotiation for the session; clause 7.1.3.1.3 has the MC service server determine the participants list itself, based on criteria from the initiating MC service client, again negotiating SDP for the ad hoc session.

question: Which procedures put the MAP protocol and the MSC in the same step for handling an inter-node handover or emergency-call location request?
reference_answer: TS 29.010 4.5 (Inter-MSC Handover): interworking rules govern whether new handover parameters are carried in the AN-APDU (same encapsulated protocol as the target radio access network interface) or in a MAP message (different encapsulated protocol, or parameters needed only by the target MSC) when transferred over the E-interface between MSCs. TS 32.271 5.2.3.3 (Network Induced Location Request): during an emergency call, the MSC (or SGSN) forwards the location request to the GMLC via a MAP Subscriber Location Report, which the GMLC acknowledges before transferring the location information to the LCS client.

question: Which procedures put the IMS-ALG and the GW in the same step for Optimal Media Routeing session establishment?
reference_answer: TS 32.260 5.2.2.1.19.1 (IMS-ALG bypasses its local GW): the IMS-ALG allocates a local transport address at a GW then, once OMR selects the same IP realm as the incoming leg, de-allocates that GW so the local GW is bypassed. TS 32.260 5.2.2.1.19.2 (alternate IP realm is selected): the IMS-ALG interacts with a first GW and an alternate GW, then de-allocates the first GW and maintains the user-plane connection through the alternate GW when OMR selects a different realm.

question: Which procedure puts the WT and the WLAN in the same step for modifying resources of an existing LWA bearer?
reference_answer: TS 36.300 22A.1.7.2 (WT Modification): either the eNB or the WT can initiate WT Modification to modify, establish or release bearer contexts for WLAN resources within the same WT; the eNB and WT exchange WT Modification Request/Confirm (or Required/Acknowledge) messages and the eNB reconfigures the UE's RRC connection if needed.

question: Which procedures put the CHF and the NSSAI in the same step for determining Network Slice charging duration by tenant?
reference_answer: TS 32.847 6.7.2.3 (Flow description): for NS actual duration charging based on SMF reporting, the CHF acting as UE CCS generates the UE CDR per S-NSSAI and reports each PDU session establishment/release Charging Data Request to the CHF acting as Tenant CCS, which generates CDRs the billing domain uses to derive the NS actual duration for the tenant. TS 32.847 6.7.4.3 (Flow description): for NS actual duration charging based on NWDAF performance collection, the CEF subscribes to PDU session count changes from the NWDAF and, once it determines the NS duration from the reported status, triggers a Charging Data Request to the CHF acting as Tenant CCS (configured with the S-NSSAI-to-Tenant-ID relationship), which counts the duration of the network slice for the tenant.

question: Which procedures put the SEAF, the UDM and the AUSF in the same step for EAP-TLS based primary authentication?
reference_answer: TS 33.501 B.2.1.1 (Security procedures, EAP-TLS): the SEAF forwards the UE's SUCI to the AUSF via Nausf_UEAuthentication_Authenticate; the AUSF requests authentication data from the UDM via Nudm_UEAuthentication_Get, the UDM (SIDF) de-conceals the SUCI and selects EAP-TLS, and the SEAF then relays every subsequent EAP-TLS message between the UE and the AUSF until the AUSF derives KAUSF/KSEAF and the SEAF derives KAMF. TS 33.501 O.3 (Authentication procedure): for a non-5G-capable (N5GC) device registering via a W-AGF, the AMF/SEAF selects the AUSF and sends Nausf_UEAuthentication_Authenticate Request; the AUSF requests data from the UDM via Nudm_UEAuthentication_Get, the UDM selects EAP-TLS, and the SEAF relays every EAP-TLS message between the W-AGF/N5GC device and the AUSF until the AUSF derives the MSK and confirms the result to the UDM via Nudm_UEAuthentication_ResultConfirmation.

question: Which procedure puts the NG and the AN in the same step for resuming the user plane connection of a PDU session after UE-triggered connection resume?
reference_answer: TS 29.502 5.2.2.3.25 (UE Triggered Connection Resume in RRC Inactive procedure): upon a notification that the UE is reachable, the NF service consumer (e.g. AMF) requests the SMF to resume the user plane connection of a PDU session, including N2 SM information such as the Path Switch Request Transfer received from the 5G-AN (NG interface), and the SMF replies with N2 SM information (Path Switch Response Transfer) to the 5G-AN if the resume succeeds.

question: Which procedure puts the AMF, the UDM and the SNPN in the same step for updating AMF registration information for 3GPP access?
reference_answer: TS 29.503 5.3.2.2.2 (AMF registration for 3GPP access): the AMF sends a PUT request to the UDM to update or create the UE's AMF registration information, including an 'ueSnpnSubscriptionInd' IE when the UE supports equivalent SNPNs and is served by an AMF in an equivalent SNPN of its subscribed SNPN; the UDM stores or replaces the registration data and returns 200 OK/204 No Content/201 Created, or 403 Forbidden if e.g. the UE registers in an SNPN using Credentials-Holder credentials it is not authorized to use.

question: Which procedures put the AF and the NWDAF in the same step across the Data Collection AF subscription, exposure and unsubscription lifecycle?
reference_answer: TS 26.531 5.3 (subscription): both the NWDAF and the Event Consumer AF discover the Data Collection AF via Nnrf_NFDiscovery and subscribe to events using Naf_EventExposure_Subscribe. TS 26.531 5.6 (data exposure): the Data Collection AF exposes events to the NWDAF and to the Event Consumer AF via Naf_EventExposure_Notify. TS 26.531 5.7 (unsubscription): the NWDAF and the Event Consumer AF each unsubscribe from the Data Collection AF via Naf_EventExposure_Unsubscribe.

question: Which procedures put the MBMS, the BM and the SC in the same step for the MBMS User Service initiation and termination lifecycle?
reference_answer: TS 26.346 5.3.1 (Initiation): the MBMS UE registers to the MBMS User Service and requests MBMS service keys if security is activated, then uses the MBMS activation procedure to activate the MBMS Bearer Service (the BM-SC receives the activation message unless MBMS Broadcast Mode is used, in which case activation is local to the UE). TS 26.346 5.3.2 (Termination): the MBMS UE deregisters and deregisters the security association if required, then uses the MBMS deactivation procedure to deactivate the Bearer Service when no other User Service still uses it (again with no message to the BM-SC in Broadcast Mode).

question: Which procedures put the SRNC, the DRNC and the DCH in the same step for an unsynchronised transport channel bandwidth reconfiguration?
reference_answer: TS 25.931 7.14.2.2 (Bandwidth Increase): the SRNC decides no synchronised reconfiguration is needed and requests the DRNC to reconfigure the DCH via Radio Link Reconfiguration Request; both the DRNC's and the SRNC's own Node Bs allocate resources and confirm, then the SRNC sends RRC Transport Channel Reconfiguration to the UE. TS 25.931 7.14.2.3 (Bandwidth Decrease): the same SRNC-to-DRNC DCH reconfiguration request/response flow occurs, and the SRNC additionally initiates transport bearer modification of the Iub/Iur Data Transport Bearers using the ALCAP protocol.

question: Which procedures put the SRNC and the SCCP protocol in the same step for establishing an inter-RNC signalling connection to request dedicated or common resources?
reference_answer: TS 25.420 4.5.1.3 (Establishment procedure initiated from the SRNC): the SRNC sends an SCCP Connection Request carrying a RADIO LINK SETUP REQUEST or ENHANCED RELOCATION REQUEST to the DRNC to request a dedicated DCH, and the DRNC replies with SCCP Connection Confirm or Connection Refusal (RNSAP procedures per TS 25.423). TS 25.420 4.5.1.3A (initiated from an RNC requesting common measurements or information): RNC1 sends an SCCP Connection Request carrying a COMMON MEASUREMENT INITIATION REQUEST or INFORMATION EXCHANGE INITIATION REQUEST to RNC2, which replies with SCCP Connection Confirm or Refusal.

question: Which procedures put the NEF and the TMGI process in the same step, for creating or deleting an MBS session?
reference_answer: TS 23.247 clause 7.1.1.2 (MBS Session Creation without PCC) shows the AF requesting TMGI allocation from the NEF/MBSF, which forwards the request to the MB-SMF and returns the allocated TMGI(s) to the AF; the NEF/MBSF also forwards the MBS session creation request that may reference a previously allocated TMGI. Clause 7.1.1.4 (MBS Session Deletion without PCC) shows the AF optionally requesting the NEF/MBSF to de-allocate the TMGI, with the NEF/MBSF forwarding the de-allocation request to the MB-SMF and relaying the response back to the AF.

question: Which procedures put the DAA function and the UAV in the same step, for detect-and-avoid support?
reference_answer: TS 23.255 clause 7.7.2.1.1 (DAA support management procedure) shows the UAS application specific server sending a DAA support management request identifying the UAV to the UAE server, which stores the DAA application policy and executes DAA configuration for that UAV. Clause 7.7.2.2.1 (DAA support involving UAVs with U2X support) shows the UAE client detecting nearby UAVs via U2X and sending DAA client event information about them to the UAE server. Clause 7.7.2.2.2 (DAA support involving UAVs without U2X support) shows the UAS application specific server determining nearby UAVs and sending DAA server event information, including their location, to the UAE server and client.

question: In the study on NWDAF Phase 3 enhancements, which solutions put NWDAF and ADRF in the same step for trained ML model storage and retrieval?
reference_answer: TR 23.700-81 clause 6.42.2.1 ("Procedure for trained ML model(s) storage in ADRF") and clause 6.42.2.2 ("Procedure for trained ML model(s) retrieval from ADRF") both put NWDAF (containing MTLF/AnLF) and ADRF in the same step: in 6.42.2.1 the NWDAF containing MTLF sends Nadrf_MLModelManagement_StorageRequest to the ADRF and the ADRF may subscribe for ML model training updates back to the NWDAF; in 6.42.2.2 the NWDAF containing AnLF sends Nadrf_MLModelManagement_RetrievalRequest to the ADRF, which in turn discovers/queries the NWDAF containing MTLF and returns the model to the requesting NWDAF. Clause 6.43.2 ("Procedure of ML model storage in ADRF and ML model provision from ADRF") describes an alternate solution for the same storage-and-retrieval mechanism: the NWDAF containing MTLF stores the trained ML model(s) in the ADRF (optionally via DCCF) using the same Nadrf_MLModelManagement_StorageRequest operation, registers the ML model profile, and an ML model consumer (NWDAF containing AnLF) later subscribes to and retrieves it. Clause 6.61.2.1 ("Procedure for ML model Retrieval From ADRF") describes a further alternate solution where the NWDAF containing MTLF retrieves ML model(s) from the ADRF on behalf of an NWDAF containing AnLF, adjusting filter information as needed, and may store a newly trained model back to the ADRF.

question: In the study on 5G timing resiliency and time-synchronization enhancements, which procedures put ASTI and TSCTSF in the same step for AF-requested access stratum timing synchronization?
reference_answer: TR 23.700-25 clause 6.7.3.2 ("Procedure for AF requested 5G access stratum timing synchronization with Requested Coverage Area") and clause 6.18.3.2 ("Procedure for subscription based control of access stratum time synchronization service with AF request") both put ASTI and TSCTSF in the same step: the TSCTSF activates or deactivates the 5G access-stratum time-synchronization (ASTI) service for the UE based on the AF request and, respectively, the UE's presence in the requested coverage area or the UE's Time Synchronization Subscription Data and PCF policy decision.

question: In the study on 5G timing resiliency and UPF-selection enhancements, which procedures put BSF and PCF in the same step for storing UPF information in the BSF?
reference_answer: TR 23.700-62 clauses 6.15.3.1.2 ("Procedure of UPF information in BSF") and 6.22.3.2 ("The consumer NF subscribes UPF change notification from the BSF by storing UPF ID and UE IP address in the BSF...") both put BSF and PCF in the same step: during PDU Session Establishment the SMF sends Npcf_SMPolicyControl_Update to the PCF with the UE IP address and UPF ID, and the PCF then sends Nbsf_Management_Register to the BSF to store that UPF/UE-IP mapping.

question: For activating and deactivating SMS service authorization, which procedures put the AMF, the SMSF and the UDM in the same step?
reference_answer: Two procedures in TS 29.540 put the AMF, SMSF and UDM in the same step: clause 5.2.2.2.2 ('Activation of SMS service'), where the AMF sends an HTTP PUT to the SMSF to activate SMS for a UE and, if no UE Context for SMS yet exists, the SMSF registers itself with the UDM for the access type and retrieves subscription data; and clause 5.2.2.3.3 ('Removal of SMS service authorization over one of the access types'), where the AMF sends an HTTP PUT to deactivate SMS for one access type and the SMSF deregisters itself from the UDM for that access type.

question: In the enhanced network slicing study (TS 23.700-41), which procedures put the AMF and NSSF together in the same step of registration/slice selection handling?
reference_answer: In TS 23.700-41 (study on enhanced support of network slicing), five candidate solutions show the AMF and the NSSF acting together in one step of registration or slice-selection handling: clause 6.10.2 (handling of a temporary S-NSSAI, where the AMF registers to the UDM and the validity timer for a temporary S-NSSAI can also be provided by the NSSF), clause 6.25.3 (UE registration/registration-update procedure, where the AMF decides the Registration Area and Allowed NSSAI with the help of UDM/NSSF), clause 6.26.3 (registration procedure impacts, where the AMF provides NSSAI information to the NSSF and creates Allowed/Secondary Allowed NSSAI based on NSSF input), clause 6.36.3 (registration with S-NSSAI having different reasons, where the AMF, or the NSSF, determines the Allowed NSSAI), and clause 6.42.3 (replacing an unavailable S-NSSAI, where the AMF, together with the NSSF via Nnssf_NSSelection_Get, determines and configures an alternative S-NSSAI).

question: In AM and UE Policy Association handling with the PCF, which procedures put the AMF together with the CHF in the same step?
reference_answer: TS 23.502 clause 4.16.1.2 (AM Policy Association Establishment with new selected PCF) has the AMF establish the AM Policy Association while the PCF, if it determines the decision depends on policy-counter status, initiates Spending Limit Report Retrieval from the CHF before responding to the AMF. Clause 4.16.3.2 (AMF-initiated AM Policy Association Termination) has the AMF send Npcf_AMPolicyControl_Delete, after which the PCF unsubscribes from the CHF's policy counter status reporting if it had subscribed. Clause 4.16.11.1 (UE Policy Association Establishment) has the AMF establish the UE Policy Association with the (V-)PCF, and in the non-roaming case the (H-)PCF may interact with the CHF to decide UE policy based on spending limits, again via Spending Limit Report Retrieval.

question: During N2/Xn handover of a PDU session, which procedures put the AMF, SMF, and access network in the same step?
reference_answer: TS 29.502 clause 5.2.2.2.4 (I-SMF Insertion, Change or Removal during Xn based Handover) shows the NF Service Consumer (e.g. AMF) requesting the I-SMF/SMF to create an SM context using N2 SM information from the target/source 5G-AN. Clause 5.2.2.3.15 (Connection Suspend procedure) shows the AMF requesting the SMF to suspend the user plane connection using N2 SM information received from the 5G-AN. Clause 5.2.2.3.4.2 (N2 Handover Preparation) shows the target AMF requesting the SMF to prepare the handover, exchanging N2 SM information carrying resource-setup/handover-request information to and from the target 5G-AN. Clause 5.2.2.3.4.3 (N2 Handover Execution) shows the target AMF requesting the SMF to complete the handover execution, using N2 SM information from the source/target 5G-AN.

question: For layer-triggered mobility (LTM), which procedures put the gNB-CU and gNB-DU in the same step?
reference_answer: TS 38.401 clause 8.2.1.4 (Intra-gNB-DU LTM) shows the gNB-CU sending UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST messages to the gNB-DU to prepare candidate cells and later a CU-DU MOBILITY INITIATION REQUEST to trigger early synchronization/cell switch, with the gNB-DU forwarding RRC messages and reporting ACCESS SUCCESS. Clause 8.2.1.5 (Inter-gNB-DU LTM) shows the gNB-CU coordinating with both the source and candidate gNB-DUs via UE CONTEXT SETUP/MODIFICATION and CU-DU/DU-CU CELL SWITCH NOTIFICATION and TA INFORMATION TRANSFER messages when the UE moves to another gNB-DU. Clause 8.2.1.6 (LTM with gNB-CU-UP change) shows the gNB-CU-CP performing LTM configuration with the gNB-DU (steps drawn from 8.2.1.5) while also setting up/modifying the bearer context in the gNB-CU-UP.

question: For registering an IP-SM-GW with the UDM, which procedures put the UDM and the IP-SM-GW in the same step?
reference_answer: TS 29.503 clause 5.3.2.2.7 (IP-SM-GW registration) shows the HSS sending a PUT request to the UDM to create or update the UE's IP-SM-GW registration, with the UDM responding '201 Created' or '200 OK' accordingly. Clause 5.3.2.5.11 (IP-SM-GW Registration Information Retrieval) shows an NF service consumer sending a GET request to the UDM to retrieve the UE's IP-SM-GW registration information, with the UDM responding '200 OK' including the registration data.

question: Under CUPS, which node provisions the CC-POI in the SGW-U/PGW-U, over which interface, and what triggers the interception of a given IP packet?
reference_answer: Under CUPS, the CC-POI in the SGW-U/PGW-U is provisioned by the CC-TF in the SGW-C/PGW-C, using a Triggering message (i.e. ActivateTask message) sent over the LI_T3 interface. Interception of a given IP packet is triggered when the packet matches the criteria specified in that Triggering message.

question: For a PSS client that supports 360 VR video over DASH, which video media profile receiver is mandatory, which is only recommended, and which is purely optional?
reference_answer: For a PSS client supporting 360 VR video over DASH: the Basic Video Media Profile Receiver (per TS 26.118 clause 5.2.2.3) is mandatory ("shall"); the Main Video Media Profile Receiver (clause 5.2.3.3) is recommended ("should"); and the Advanced Video Media Profile Receiver (clause 5.2.3.4) is purely optional ("may").
