question: When a Timing Advance Command addressed with a PUR-RNTI arrives and a stored NTA exists, what must the MAC entity do with the pur-TimeAlignmentTimer and what must it tell the upper layers?
reference_answer: When a Timing Advance Command MAC control element or PDCCH indicating timing advance adjustment addressed with a PUR-RNTI is received and an NTA has been stored, the MAC entity shall apply the Timing Advance Command/adjustment, start or restart the pur-TimeAlignmentTimer if configured, and indicate to upper layers that the Timing Advance value has been adjusted.

question: What do the two values of the RQI flag mean, and what must the NG-RAN node do with the indicator when Reflective QoS Activation was never configured for that QoS flow?
reference_answer: RQI set to 0 means deactivate Reflective QoS; RQI set to 1 means activate Reflective QoS. If Reflective QoS Activation (RQA) has not been configured for the involved QoS flow, the RQI shall be ignored by the NG-RAN node.

question: How many UTRA carriers must be used when testing a single-carrier capable base station, and against what declared information are the multi-carrier test configurations constructed?
reference_answer: A single UTRA carrier must be used for testing a single-carrier capable base station. For other BS types, the multi-carrier test configurations (UTCx, per TS 25.141 clause 4.12) are constructed subject to the parameters declared by the manufacturer for the supported RF configurations.

question: In the PDN GW initiated resource allocation deactivation over S2b, what happens to the other bearers when the default bearer of a PDN connection is deactivated, and is the PDN address released during a handover?
reference_answer: If the default bearer belonging to a PDN connection is deactivated, the PDN GW deactivates all bearers belonging to that PDN connection. When performed for a handover, the connections associated with the PDN address are released, but the PDN address itself is kept in the PDN GW (i.e. not released).

question: If the requesting UE gets no keepalive response after the maximum retransmissions of T4101, which procedure must it start instead, and what must a remote UE additionally initiate?
reference_answer: If no response is received after reaching the maximum number of allowed retransmissions of T4101, the requesting UE shall abort the link keepalive procedure and initiate the direct link release procedure instead. If the requesting UE is a remote UE, it shall additionally initiate the relay reselection procedure.

question: On receiving a REFER request within a dialog, what role must the MSC Server take on behalf of the UE, and why is acceptance made subject to operator policy?
reference_answer: The MSC Server shall act as a transferee on behalf of the UE. Acceptance is subject to operator policy because CS domain access signalling does not provide a mechanism to present the transfer request to the transferee for authorization, so automatic acceptance and execution of the REFER request can pose a security risk or have unwanted charging consequences.

question: If a WLCP entity receives a STATUS message with cause #81 Invalid PTI value, what must it abort and what must it stop?
reference_answer: It must abort any ongoing WLCP procedure related to the received PTI value and stop any related timer.

question: For CLI-RSSI in frequency range 1, where is the reference point, and what constraint applies to the reported value when the UE uses receiver diversity?
reference_answer: For frequency range 1, the reference point for CLI-RSSI is the antenna connector of the UE. If receiver diversity is in use by the UE, the reported CLI-RSSI value shall not be lower than the corresponding CLI-RSSI of any of the individual receiver branches.

question: On the first expiry of timer T3595 at the TWAG, what must it resend and what must it restart?
reference_answer: On the first expiry of timer T3595, the TWAG shall resend the PDN DISCONNECT REQUEST message and shall reset and restart timer T3595.

question: If the UE does not support simultaneousRxDataSSB-DiffNumerology, what restriction applies to CSI-RS measurement for L1-SINR?
reference_answer: The UE is required to measure only one of CSI-RS for L1-SINR measurement and SSB, not both; a longer measurement period for CSI-RS based L1-SINR measurement is expected, and no requirements are defined.

question: Which transport protocol must carry ProSe messages between the UE and the Key Management Function, and which HTTP method is used for the procedures?
reference_answer: HTTP 1.1 (as specified in IETF RFC 2616) must carry ProSe messages between the UE and the ProSe Key Management Function, and HTTP POST methods are used for the procedures.

question: In the CMPv2 profile for PKIMessage, how many PKIMessages may a single message contain, and is the protection field optional?
reference_answer: All CMPv2 messages used within this profile shall consist of exactly one PKIMessage (the sequence size shall be 1 in all cases). The protection field of type PKIProtection is optional in the RFC but its support and usage is required by this profile.

question: For a Certification Request, which private key must the NF sign the PKIMessage with, and what must the extraCerts field contain?
reference_answer: The PKIMessage sent by the NF shall be signed with the private key related to one of the valid operator provided NF certificates. The mandatory extraCerts field shall contain the NF certificate related to the signing private key, plus any intermediate CA certificates if the NF certificate is not signed directly by a root CA.

question: When a web server uses CGI or other scripting, what restriction applies to the upload directory?
reference_answer: The associated CGI/script directory shall not be used for uploads — the upload directory must be different from the CGI/Scripting directory.

question: What must a manufacturer declare regarding UTRA FDD coexistence, and how does each answer affect testing obligations?
reference_answer: The manufacturer shall declare whether the BS is intended to operate in geographic areas where UTRA FDD is also deployed, and whether it is intended to operate co-located with a UTRA FDD BS. If the first is declared, compliance with subclause 6.6.3.2.4.1 is mandatory (otherwise not tested); if the second is declared, compliance with subclause 6.6.3.2.4.2 is mandatory (otherwise not tested).

question: During network slice replacement, under what circumstance does the AMF release a PDU session instead of retaining it with the alternative S-NSSAI?
reference_answer: The AMF releases the PDU session instead of retaining it with the alternative S-NSSAI if it determines the PDU session cannot be retained with the alternative S-NSSAI for some reason, e.g. the V-SMF/I-SMF cannot support the alternative S-NSSAI.

question: Which two alternatives may the consumer supply for data forwarding during 5GS to EPS idle mode mobility over N26?
reference_answer: The consumer may supply the forwardingFTeid received from the MME in the Context Acknowledge, if any, or the forwarding bearer contexts received from the MME in the Context Acknowledge, if any.

question: For SL PRS in sidelink resource allocation mode 1, which clause's procedure must the UE follow for a dedicated resource pool, and what substitution applies?
reference_answer: The UE shall follow the procedure described in clause 8.6 (excluding the case of PSSCH for retransmission of a transport block). The substitutions applied are: "PSSCH for a transport block" is replaced by "SL PRS", and "PSSCH" is replaced by "SL PRS".

question: For frequency range 2, how must CLI-RSSI be measured with respect to antenna elements?
reference_answer: For frequency range 2, CLI-RSSI shall be measured based on the combined signal from antenna elements corresponding to a given receiver branch.

question: Full ICE functionality is optional for the IBCF and the TrGW. If a vendor nevertheless claims ICE support, what is the minimum ICE variant both entities must implement?
reference_answer: Both the IBCF and the TrGW shall at least support ICE lite as specified in IETF RFC 8445.

question: Two networks connected via CS-IBCF and CS-TrGW sit in different IP realms. Is IP realm indication mandatory for both entities, and how must the CS-TrGW react if the available IP realms change?
reference_answer: Yes, the CS-IBCF and the CS-TrGW shall support IP realm indication. If there is a change in the IP Realms that are available or if they are modified in the CS-TrGW, the CS-TrGW shall inform the CS-IBCF via the IP Realm Availability Procedure, if this procedure is supported by the CS-TrGW.

question: For a PFCP Request message, which IP address must appear as destination and which as source, and can the destination address agreed for a PFCP session be changed later?
reference_answer: The IP Destination Address of a Request message shall be an IP address of the peer entity, and the IP Source Address shall be an IP address of the sending entity. Yes, the CP and UP functions may change the destination address subsequently during a PFCP Session Modification procedure.

question: A UP function receives a GTP-U Error Indication message. Which procedure must it start towards the CP function, and which two IEs of the Error Indication must be reported?
reference_answer: The UP function shall initiate a PFCP Session Report procedure towards the CP function, sending an Error Indication Report that includes the remote F-TEID signalled in the GTP-U Peer Address IE and the Tunnel Endpoint Identifier Data I IE of the GTP-U Error Indication.

question: Which content types must be supported for the Nudr_GroupIDmap-related HTTP bodies, and which content type signals the use of JSON Merge Patch in a request body?
reference_answer: JSON, the Problem Details JSON Object, JSON Merge Patch, and JSON Patch content types must be supported. The content type "application/merge-patch+json" signals the use of JSON Merge Patch in a request body.

question: For a UE attached over untrusted non-3GPP access using IPSec tunnel mode, what must it subtract from the path MTU to the ePDG before selecting the SIP transport, and why?
reference_answer: The UE must subtract (decrement) the IPSec tunnel overhead from the path MTU between the UE and the ePDG prior to applying the transport selection for SIP requests, in order to reduce the risk of UDP fragmentation.

question: When a UE transitions between DRX and no DRX, which evaluation period must it apply to each BFD-RS resource during the transition window, and which one afterwards?
reference_answer: During the transition window (a duration equal to the evaluation period of the second mode), the UE shall use an evaluation period no less than the minimum of the evaluation periods corresponding to the first and second modes, for each BFD-RS resource. Afterwards, it shall use the evaluation period corresponding to the second mode.

question: Is a UE required to use measurement gaps to measure SSB for beam failure detection, and in FR1 what happens when the SSB for BFD and the CSI-RS share an OFDM symbol with the same SCS?
reference_answer: No, the UE is required to be capable of measuring SSB for BFD without measurement gaps. In FR1, if the SSB for BFD and CSI-RS share the same OFDM symbol and have the same SCS, the UE shall be able to measure the SSB for BFD without any restriction.

question: A manufacturer declares that the BS under test is intended to operate co-sited with another TDD or FDD BS having uplink receive functionality on an adjacent frequency. Which ACLR conformance subclause becomes mandatory, and which one need not be tested if the declaration is negative?
reference_answer: Conformance with the ACLR requirement specified in subclause 6.6.2.2.2.3 becomes mandatory. If the declaration is negative (not co-sited), that same requirement (subclause 6.6.2.2.2.3) need not be tested.

question: The UTRAN cannot support any of the ciphering or integrity protection algorithms carried in a SECURITY MODE COMMAND. Which message must go back to the CN and with which cause value, and what cause is used instead when the radio interface procedure itself fails?
reference_answer: The UTRAN shall return a SECURITY MODE REJECT message to the CN with cause value "Requested Ciphering and/or Integrity Protection Algorithms not Supported". If the radio interface Security Mode Control procedure itself fails, the SECURITY MODE REJECT message shall instead carry cause value "Failure in the Radio Interface Procedure".

question: May a vendor use the Iur private message mechanism to carry basic functionality, and what are the two purposes for which it is allowed?
reference_answer: No, the private message mechanism shall not be used for basic functionality (which shall be standardised). It may be used for special operator/vendor-specific features not considered part of basic functionality, and for vendor research purposes, e.g. to implement and evaluate new algorithms/features before proposing them for standardisation.

question: An RNC uses the IP transport option over slow E1/T1/J1 PPP links. Which two extra capabilities must it support, and how must header compression be negotiated over PPP?
reference_answer: It shall also support IP Header Compression (RFC 2507) and the PPP extensions ML/MC-PPP (RFC 1990, RFC 2686). Negotiation of header compression over PPP shall be performed via RFC 2509.

question: For the Iur IP option, which IP version must a UTRAN node support and which is optional, and which four fields identify the transport bearer?
reference_answer: An IP UTRAN node shall support IPv6; support of IPv4 is optional. The transport bearer is identified by the source UDP port number, destination UDP port number, source IP address, and destination IP address.

question: When the Lower Layer presence status change IE is set to "release lower layers" or "suspend lower layers", which resources and contexts must still be kept, and after which prior value may "re-establish lower layers" be set?
reference_answer: PDCP entities, X2-U bearer resources, S1-U bearer resources and UE context information shall be kept. "re-establish lower layers" shall only be set after "release lower layers" has previously been indicated.

question: If a UE-associated signalling connection over X2 was set up including the eNB UE X2AP ID Extension, for how long and by which peers must that extension be used?
reference_answer: The eNB UE X2AP ID Extension shall be used by both peers for the life-time of the respective UE-associated signalling connection.

question: Subscriber A activates a CCBS request against destination B. Which two queues must HLR A inspect to detect an identical request already existing, and why both?
reference_answer: HLR A shall check subscriber A's originating queue for any previous requests activated by subscriber A against destination B for the same basic service group, and shall also check subscriber A's target queue for any requests activated by destination B against subscriber A for the same basic service group — because checking for an identical CCBS request must include checks in both directions.

question: Destination B activates Call Forwarding on Busy after subscriber A has already activated a CCBS request against B. What must HLR B do with the queued requests, and which two network provider options exist when a CCBS call later reaches MSC B with MS B NDUB?
reference_answer: HLR B shall continue to process CCBS Requests in the queue. When a CCBS call subsequently arrives at MSC B and MS B is NDUB, a network provider option exists: either the CCBS call is treated as when MS B is busy for the CCBS call without CFB active, or the CCBS call is forwarded without the CCBS call Indicator.

question: How many streams must each termination in a conference context support and for which media, and from how many through-connected terminations must the MRFP treat the context as an ad-hoc conference?
reference_answer: Each termination shall support up to three streams: one for audio, one for messaging, and one for video. The MRFP shall consider the context to represent an ad-hoc conference when three or more terminations have been through-connected.

question: If a UE decides to use TLS for MBMS key management, is a ciphersuite with NULL encryption allowed, and is support of certificate revocation mandatory?
reference_answer: No, when the UE decides to use TLS, use of a TLS ciphersuite without NULL encryption is mandatory (a NULL-encryption ciphersuite is not allowed). Support of certificate revocation is optional, not mandatory.

question: For EVS error concealment, what must the decoder be informed about before concealment actions start, and which kind of substitute frame is explicitly not allowed?
reference_answer: The decoder shall be informed about erroneous/lost frames so that error concealment actions can be initiated, using a set of predicted parameters in the speech synthesis. Insertion of speech signal independent silence frames is not allowed.

question: A concrete NRM class is mapped to YANG. What must the grouping and the list be named, which attribute serves as the key, and where must all the other attributes be placed?
reference_answer: The grouping shall be named <IocName>Grp and the list shall be named <IocName>. The NamingAttribute shall be used as the key. All other attributes shall be placed inside a non-presence "container" named "attributes".

question: In pull-mode IUT replication over the roaming II-NNI, which method parameter value must the Refer-To header field of the REFER request carry, and which option tag has to populate its Require header field?
reference_answer: The Refer-To header field must carry the method parameter set to "MESSAGE", and the Require header field must be populated with the option tag value "tdialog".

question: For push-mode replication at the roaming II-NNI, what must the Accept-Contact header field of the REFER request carry alongside the g.3gpp.iut-focus media feature tag, and which header fields must the embedded Refer-To content include?
reference_answer: The Accept-Contact header field must carry the "g.3gpp.iut-focus" media feature tag with explicit and require tags. The embedded Refer-To content must include the Accept-Contact header field, the P-Preferred-Service header field, and the "application/sdp" MIME body.

question: An NPN-capable UE camping on an NPN-only cell receives SIB9 carrying eventID-TSS. From which SIB1 list entry must it derive the gNB identity and PLMN identity, and does the same source apply to a UE on an ordinary PLMN cell?
reference_answer: It must derive the gNB identity from gNB-ID-Length and cellIdentity of the first NPN-IdentityInfo list entry of NPN-IdentityInfoList in SIB1, and derive the plmn-Identity from the first NPN-Identity list entry of NPN-IdentityList within that same NPN-IdentityInfo entry. No — for a UE on an ordinary PLMN cell, the source is instead the first PLMN-IdentityInfo list entry of PLMN-IdentityInfoList in SIB1, for both the gNB identity and the plmn-Identity.

question: If the UE has already stored some SIB23 segments and the SIB23 value tag then changes, what must it do with those stored segments before storing the new one?
reference_answer: The UE shall discard all stored segments before storing the new one.

question: When a UE needs to send E-UTRA MR-DC dedicated information such as an MCGFailureInformation message, which field of the ULInformationTransferMRDC message must it populate, and which field would carry NR-related dedicated information instead?
reference_answer: It must populate the ul-DCCH-MessageNR field. The ul-DCCH-MessageEUTRA field would instead carry E-UTRA-related dedicated information (e.g. E-UTRA RRC MeasurementReport or MCGFailureInformation).

question: On receiving an RRCReconfigurationCompleteSidelink that contains sl-DRX-ConfigReject, which timer must the UE stop for that destination and what does it conclude about sidelink DRX for the unicast link?
reference_answer: The UE must stop timer T400 for that destination. It concludes that no sidelink DRX is to be applied for the corresponding sidelink unicast communication.

question: When several HS-PDSCHs are sent to one UE in the same cell, what must hold for their transmit powers, and which channels are counted together in the total-power limit signalled by higher layers?
reference_answer: All the HS-PDSCHs intended for that UE shall be transmitted with equal power. The total-power limit counts together HS-PDSCHs, HS-SCCHs, E-AGCHs, E-RGCHs and E-HICHs in the cell.

question: For a UE in soft handover receiving several E-HICH ACK/NACKs in one E-DCH TTI, which of those indications must be soft-combined before being handed to higher layers, and what happens when a radio link set holds only one radio link?
reference_answer: ACK/NACKs from the same radio link set must be soft combined into one ACK/NACK information before being delivered to higher layers. If a radio link set contains only one radio link, detection is done as for a UE not in soft handover (no combining).

question: A MExE classmark 2 device supports the JavaPhone Power Monitor package. Which two battery events must it generate as a minimum, and are the remaining Power Monitor events mandatory or merely recommended?
reference_answer: It must at least generate BatteryCritical (when the battery is at a critically low level) and BatteryNormal (when the battery is no longer low). All the other Power Monitor events are merely recommended ("should be supported"), not mandatory.

question: To bring a non-current full native EPS security context back into use after handover from GERAN or UTRAN, which procedure must the UE and MME run, and what must the MME do before the NAS COUNT wraps around?
reference_answer: The UE and the MME must run a NAS SMC (Security Mode Command) procedure. Before the NAS uplink or downlink COUNT wraps around with the current security context, the MME shall activate fresh NAS keys from an EPS AKA run or activate a native security context with sufficiently low NAS COUNT values.

question: When an eNB turns on user plane integrity protection while adding a DRB, how must it choose the NR integrity algorithm relative to the EPS algorithm it had signalled in the AS Security Mode Command, and what does 128-EIA2 map onto?
reference_answer: The eNB shall select the NR integrity algorithm (NIA) that corresponds to the EPS integrity algorithm (EIA) it selected and indicated to the UE in the AS Security Mode Command procedure. 128-EIA2 maps onto 128-NIA2.

question: For an analogue connection to the POI, what nominal SJLR and RJLR values apply, and what limits constrain the RJLR at the maximum and minimum settings of a user-controlled receiving volume control?
reference_answer: The nominal values are SJLR = 0 ± 3 dB and RJLR = 0 ± 3 dB. When the user-controlled receiving volume control is set to maximum, the RJLR shall not be ≤ -15 dB, and when set to minimum, the RJLR shall not be ≥ 16 dB.

question: Which of the four alternatives for obtaining SACH metadata fragments is the default one an MBMS Client must use, and which element with its child must the USBD describing the SACH contain?
reference_answer: The default alternative is alternative d), where the MBMS Client constructs the bootstrap URL from MNC and MCC. The USBD describing the SACH shall contain the requiredCapabilities element with its feature child element.

question: In the E-UTRAN Allocation and Retention Priority IE, what does Priority Level 15 mean, how are values 1 to 14 ordered, and how must a received value of 0 be treated?
reference_answer: Priority Level 15 means "no priority". Values 1 to 14 are ordered in decreasing order of priority, i.e. 1 is the highest and 14 the lowest. A received value of 0 shall be treated as a logical error.

question: If a UE has ranging and sidelink positioning configuration both pre-configured in the ME and delivered as an RSLPP by the PCF, which one wins, and where does UICC configuration sit in that precedence order?
reference_answer: The configuration provided as a RSLPP by PCF takes precedence over the ME pre-configured information, since PCF-provided RSLPP configuration is first in the precedence order (a) while ME pre-configured information is last (d). UICC-configured information sits third, between the application-server-provided configuration (via SR1) and the ME pre-configured information.

question: Before a target UE may select a discovered UE as its located UE, what must the UE role in the RSPP metadata indicate, and in which message does that metadata arrive for V2X capable UEs?
reference_answer: The UE role in the RSPP metadata must indicate that the UE supports UE role as a located UE. For V2X capable UEs, that metadata arrives in the DIRECT LINK ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT message (for non-V2X capable UEs it arrives in the PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message).

question: If a Transmission Request arriving from a transmission participant carries no Track Info field, which three values must the transmission control server interface place into the Track Info field it creates, and what does it use when the participant-type element is unavailable?
reference_answer: It must place the negotiated "mc_queueing" fmtp attribute value into the Queueing Capability value, a Participant Type value, and the temporary identifier as the first Transmission Participant Reference value. When the participant-type element is unavailable, it sets the Participant Type value to "unknown".

question: If the CP function receives a PFCP Session Report Request whose F-SEID it does not recognise, which rejection cause must it return, and when the EPFAR feature is in use what does a PSDBU flag set to 1 tell it about the session in the UP function?
reference_answer: It shall return the rejection cause "Session context not found". When the EPFAR feature is in use, a PSDBU flag set to "1" tells the CP function that the PFCP Session is locally deleted in the UP function.

question: An IMS-ALG has forwarded an SDP offer without allocating a primary local MR and now gets back an SDP answer carrying a valid connection address. If it had earlier bypassed previous MRs, what must it copy into the media line of that answer?
reference_answer: It must copy into the media line of the SDP answer the visited-realm or secondary-realm instance from the media line of the received SDP offer that was used to populate the connection address and port information in the forwarded offer, replacing the connection-address and port with those from the received SDP answer (and replacing the IP realm name with the local IP realm name if it is a connected IP realm).

question: Before user data may be carried on a PLMN traffic channel, the controlling entities have to run an end-to-end synchronization process. At which message is the "physical connection established" indication given for a mobile terminated call, and for a mobile initiated in-call modification?
reference_answer: For a mobile terminated call (MTC), the indication is given on sending the CONNECT ACKNOWLEDGE message. For a mobile initiated in-call modification, it is given on sending the MODIFY COMPLETE message (sent after reception of the ASSIGNMENT COMPLETE or RAB ASSIGNMENT RESPONSE message).

question: On the transit side towards the fixed network, what is done with circuit 108 to the selected modem at the start of timer T, and how are the remaining interchange circuits treated until timer T expires?
reference_answer: At the start of timer T, circuit 108 to the selected modem is switched from the "OFF" to "ON" condition, initiating establishment of the modem connection. The remaining interchange circuits towards the modem (except CT108) are held in the OFF condition until timer T expires, when they are switched to ON.

question: An I-MGCF supporting the PSTN XML body received two PSTN XML Bearer Capability elements in an INVITE, but the succeeding trunk does not support TMR "64 kBit/s preferred" and no matching elements arrived in the Access Transport Parameter. What must the I-MGCF build, and in which response does it place it?
reference_answer: The I-MGCF must build a PSTN XML body containing a BearerCapability element copied from the first BearerCapability element received in the PSTN XML in the INVITE, a HighLayerCompatibility element (copied from the first one received, if two were present), and a ProgressIndicator element with "Progress Description" value 5, "Coding Standard" value "00", and default "Location" value "0011 (Transit Network)". It places this PSTN XML body in the 18x Response.

question: Which received ISUP messages force the I-MGCF to send a SIP 181 Call is being forwarded, and what must the call diversion information and the optional backward call indicators show for that obligation to apply?
reference_answer: The I-MGCF sends the SIP 181 Call is being forwarded upon receiving an ACM or a CPG message. For that obligation to apply, the call diversion information must not indicate that presentation is not allowed, and the optional backward call indicators must indicate that in-band information is available.

question: An O-MGCF sent an INVITE without determining the end of address signalling and then receives a 484 Address Incomplete while Ti/w2 is running. Which timer must it start, what stops both timers, and which REL cause value is sent if that timer expires?
reference_answer: The O-MGCF must start timer Ti/w3 (if there are no other pending INVITE transactions for the call). Both Ti/w2 and Ti/w3 are stopped at the receipt of a SAM, a SIP 18x provisional response, or a SIP 200 OK (INVITE). If Ti/w3 expires, the O-MGCF sends a REL message with Cause Value 28.

question: At which node does interworking between the radio interface compatibility mechanisms and MAP take place, and what must happen when the MS signals a higher SS version than the MSC/VLR can support at all?
reference_answer: Interworking between the radio interface compatibility mechanisms and MAP occurs at the MSC/VLR. If the MS signals a higher version than the MSC/VLR is capable of supporting at all, the MSC/VLR shall attempt to support service at the highest version it does support, and if that is not possible the communication is rejected.

question: When an SCC AS supporting OMR merges media lines from a source access leg and a target access leg into one SDP offer and any of them carries OMR attributes, what is it required to do before sending the offer to the remote party?
reference_answer: It is required to recalculate the checksums as specified in subclause 5.6.3 of TS 29.079 before sending the offer to the remote party. (If it has not changed the content of an m-line and its associated attributes, it shall only calculate the session level checksum and replace the value in each occurrence of the "a=omr-s-cksum" attribute.)

question: The VLR invokes MAP_FORWARD_NEW_TMSI but at that moment there is no radio connection to the MS. What is the MSC obliged to do with the received MAP service request?
reference_answer: The MSC shall ignore the received MAP_FORWARD_NEW_TMSI request message.

question: How does a UE compute the SFN and subframe at which each RMTC occasion starts from rmtc-Periodicity and rmtc-SubframeOffset, and what is it forbidden to consider on the rmtc-Frequency?
reference_answer: The SFN and subframe are computed as: SFN mod T = FLOOR(rmtc-SubframeOffset/10), subframe = rmtc-SubframeOffset mod 10, with T = rmtc-Periodicity/10. On the rmtc-Frequency, the UE shall not consider RSSI measurements taken outside the configured RMTC occasion (which lasts for measDurationSymbols).

question: For an event-triggered report, which threshold or offset parameter does the UE take as the sorting quantity for an NR cell under eventA3 versus eventA5, and what does it use for an E-UTRA cell?
reference_answer: For an NR cell under eventA3, the UE takes the quantity used in the aN-Offset as the sorting quantity; under eventA5, it takes the quantity used in the a5-Threshold2. For an E-UTRA cell, it uses the quantity used in the bN-ThresholdEUTRA.

question: An IAB-MT in RRC_CONNECTED needs to send F1-C related information over the UL information transfer procedure. Which radio bearer must already be established before it is allowed to initiate the procedure?
reference_answer: SRB2 or split SRB2 must already be established before the IAB-MT is allowed to initiate the UL information transfer procedure to send F1-C related information.

question: On receiving a REROUTE NAS REQUEST, which IE tells the NG-RAN node where to reroute the INITIAL UE MESSAGE, and what must it do with the Allowed NSSAI IE if that IE is present?
reference_answer: The AMF Set ID IE tells the NG-RAN node where to reroute the INITIAL UE MESSAGE. If the Allowed NSSAI IE is present, the NG-RAN node shall propagate it in the rerouted INITIAL UE MESSAGE message.

question: A UE receives a TRANSPORT FORMAT COMBINATION CONTROL message on AM or UM RLC whose protocol error sets PROTOCOL_ERROR_REJECT to TRUE. Which failure message must it send, on which logical channel and RLC mode, and where does it read the RRC transaction identifier from?
reference_answer: The UE must send a TRANSPORT FORMAT COMBINATION CONTROL FAILURE message on the uplink DCCH using AM RLC. It reads the RRC transaction identifier from the value of "RRC transaction identifier" in the entry for the TRANSPORT FORMAT COMBINATION CONTROL message in the table "Rejected transactions" in the variable TRANSACTIONS.

question: After a UE discards an invalid PHYSICAL SHARED CHANNEL ALLOCATION message, which message does it submit on the uplink SHCCH, which counter is reset and which timer is started?
reference_answer: It submits the PUSCH CAPACITY REQUEST message on the uplink SHCCH. Counter V310 is reset, and timer T310 is started.

question: A COMMON TRANSPORT CHANNEL RESOURCES REQUEST carries only one of the Transport Layer Address IE and the Binding ID IE for a transport channel to be established. What must the DRNC do, and with which message?
reference_answer: The DRNC shall reject the procedure using the COMMON TRANSPORT CHANNEL RESOURCES FAILURE message.

question: In an INFORMATION TRANSFER CONTROL REQUEST on Iur, which IE decides between suspending and resuming information transfer, and which IE names the cells the control applies to?
reference_answer: The Control Type IE (indicating Suspension IE or Resume IE) decides between suspending and resuming information transfer, and the UMTS Cell Information IE within the Controlled Object Scope IE names the cells the control applies to.

question: A target eNB gets a HANDOVER REQUEST carrying a CSG Id IE but no CSG Membership Status IE, and the CSG Id does not match that of the target cell. What must it send back to the MME?
reference_answer: The target eNB shall send the HANDOVER FAILURE message to the MME with an appropriate cause value.

question: In which message must the MS always send its MS radio access capability to the SGSN irrespective of whether it is attaching in A/Gb or Iu mode, and in which later messages does the SGSN ask for the remaining radio capabilities?
reference_answer: The MS shall always send its MS radio access capability in the GPRS Attach Request message, regardless of whether it is attaching in A/Gb or Iu mode. The SGSN requests the MS's remaining radio capabilities in the Attach Complete or RA Update Complete messages.

question: What event resets and starts the READY timer in the MS and in the SGSN respectively, which state do the MM contexts fall back to when it expires, and which node alone may change its length and in which messages?
reference_answer: The READY timer is reset and begins running in the MS when an LLC PDU is transmitted, and in the SGSN when an LLC PDU is correctly received. When it expires, the MM contexts in the MS and SGSN return to STANDBY state. Only the SGSN may change the length of the READY timer, by transmitting a new value in the Attach Accept or Routeing Area Update Accept messages.

question: Once a P-TMSI Signature has been given to the MS, in which three uplink requests must the MS include it, and what should the SGSN do when the value it receives does not match the stored one?
reference_answer: The MS must include the P-TMSI Signature in the next Routeing Area Update Request, Detach Request, and Attach Request. If the value received does not match the stored one, the SGSN should use the security functions to authenticate the MS.

question: When a subscriber with CFB in registration state "Registered" attaches to a VLR, which registration parameter and which three subscription options must the HLR pass to that VLR?
reference_answer: The HLR must pass the registration parameter "forwarded-to number", and information about the subscription options "notification to the calling party", "notification to the forwarding party", and "MSISDN of the served subscriber can be presented to the forwarded-to subscriber".

question: In an Any Time Modification ack, when must the Forwarded-to number IE be present and when must the Long forwarded-to number IE be used instead?
reference_answer: The Forwarded-to number IE shall be present if at least one of the HLR and the gsmSCF does not support Long Forwarded-to Numbers (otherwise absent). The Long forwarded-to number IE shall be present if both the HLR and the gsmSCF support Long Forwarded-to Numbers (otherwise absent).

question: For EPC-routed traffic in the roaming case, what creates the V-PCRF routing information in the V-DRA and what removes it again?
reference_answer: The V-PCRF routing information (DRA binding) in the V-DRA is created when the S9 session establishment trigger is received, and it is removed when the S9 session termination notification is received.

question: For distribution of ProSe group keys, what protection must the shared and session keys get, which UEs alone may receive them, and which party must a Public Safety ProSe-enabled UE be able to authenticate?
reference_answer: The shared keys and session keys shall be protected in integrity and confidentiality during their distribution. Only authorized Public Safety ProSe-enabled UEs shall receive the shared keys. The Public Safety ProSe-enabled UE must be able to authenticate the network entity distributing the shared keys.

question: For ciphering of ProSe one-to-one traffic, which algorithms are mandatory to implement, which key is used, and what are Bearer[0]-Bearer[4] and COUNT[0]-COUNT[15] set to?
reference_answer: ProSe enabled Public Safety UEs shall implement EEA0, 128-EEA1, and 128-EEA2 (and may implement 128-EEA3) for ciphering of one-to-one traffic, using the key PEK. Bearer[0] to Bearer[4] are set to LCID, and COUNT[0] to COUNT[15] are set to KD-sess ID.

question: When certificates authenticate a ProSe Proximity Request, which single key usage bit must be set as mandatory critical, and which TS 33.310 certificate profile clauses apply to ALUID-associated certificates and to the CA certificates in the validation chain?
reference_answer: Only digitalSignature shall be set as the mandatory critical key usage. Clause 6.1.3 (SEG certificates) applies to ALUID-associated certificates, and clause 6.1.4 (SEG CA certificates) applies to any CA certificates used in a chain to validate the certificates.

question: Which procedure does the MGCF use to have the IM-MGW prepare CS network side bearer establishment, what three things does it ask the IM-MGW for, and which message does the MGCF then send to the preceding node?
reference_answer: The MGCF uses the Prepare Bearer procedure to have the IM-MGW prepare for CS network side bearer establishment. It requests the IM-MGW to provide a bearer address, a binding reference, and (optionally) notification when the bearer is established. The MGCF then sends the APM message to the preceding node.

question: Within how many seconds of end-to-end connection with the PSAP should the eCall MSD typically be available, and where eCall indicators are unsupported by the serving network, what is the limit on the PSAP modem differentiating an eCall from another TS12 call?
reference_answer: The MSD should typically be available to the PSAP within 4 seconds of end-to-end connection being established. Where eCall indicators are unsupported by the serving network, the PSAP modem's differentiation of an eCall from another TS12 call shall not exceed 2 seconds from when the IVS receives notification that the PSAP has answered the call.

question: Why can a supplementary service never be sold to a user on its own, and what must it always be offered together with?
reference_answer: A supplementary service modifies or supplements a basic telecommunication service, so it cannot be offered to a user as a stand-alone service. It shall be offered together or in association with a basic telecommunication service.

question: How are user device IP addresses normally allocated in a PLMN, when must a static address be possible instead, who assigns it, and where must the details of an assigned static address be kept?
reference_answer: User device IP addresses should normally be allocated dynamically by the network operator and managed without user intervention. For business critical applications and firewall configuration simplification, a static IP address must be possible; it shall be assigned by the network operator, and details of an assigned static IP address shall be maintained with the subscriber's records in the HLR/HSS.

question: The S4-SGSN does not itself generate charging information. When an IP-CAN session is activated and Charging Characteristics came from the HLR/HSS, what must the S4-SGSN do with them, and which value takes precedence when the PDN connection has its own Charging Characteristics?
reference_answer: If Charging Characteristics were received from the HLR/HSS, the S4-SGSN shall forward them to the S-GW as provided by the HLR/HSS, regardless of the home, visiting, or roaming case. When the PDN connection (e.g. APN) has its own Charging Characteristics present in the subscription information, that PDN-connection-specific value shall be forwarded (taking precedence); only if none is present for the PDN connection does the subscription-level Charging Characteristics get forwarded instead.

question: In which cases may an S-GW be configured to ignore the Charging Characteristics supplied by the S4-SGSN or MME for its IP-CAN bearers?
reference_answer: The S-GW may be configured to ignore the Charging Characteristics supplied by the S4-SGSN/MME in any combination of: the visiting case (S-GW and P-GW belong to the same PLMN, subscriber belongs to a different PLMN); the roaming case (P-GW belongs to a different PLMN); the home case (subscriber belongs to the same PLMN as the S-GW and P-GW); or unconditionally, i.e. it always ignores the supplied parameters.

question: Which node forwards the Charging Characteristics parameter to the TDF at IP-CAN session establishment, and in which cases may the TDF be configured to ignore them for its TDF session?
reference_answer: The P-GW forwards the Charging Characteristics parameter to the TDF (via the PCRF) at IP-CAN session establishment. The TDF may be configured to ignore the supplied Charging Characteristics in any combination of: the visiting case (subscriber belongs to a different PLMN), the roaming case (home routed traffic), the home case (subscriber belongs to the same PLMN as the TDF), or unconditionally, i.e. it always ignores the supplied parameters.

question: Which fields are mandatory in the SGSN MBMS bearer context record (S-MB-CDR), and what does the Charging ID field identify?
reference_answer: The mandatory (M) fields in the SGSN MBMS bearer context record (S-MB-CDR) are: Record Type, SGSN Address used, Charging ID, Record Opening Time, Duration, and Cause for Record Closing. The Charging ID field is the bearer context identifier used to identify this MBMS bearer context in different records created by GSNs.

question: Because the IP-Edge [PCEF] does not support individual bearers, to what do the high-level charging requirements 1 and 2 apply instead, and what must the IP-Edge be able to categorise data volumes, elapsed time and events by?
reference_answer: Since the IP-Edge [PCEF] does not support individual bearers, high-level charging requirements 1 and 2 apply to the IP-CAN session instead of an IP-CAN bearer. The IP-Edge [PCEF] shall be capable of identifying (categorising) data volumes, elapsed time, or events by QoS (as defined in TS 23.203).

question: What controls whether the In Case of Emergency dialling number file EFICE_DN is available, and what are its READ and UPDATE access conditions?
reference_answer: The availability of EFICE_DN is controlled by user/activation status: the file shall be deactivated if the user does not wish the ICE information in it to be available, and activated if the user wishes it to be available. Its access conditions are READ: ALWAYS and UPDATE: PIN.

question: What must an ITT4RT MRF assume when it receives an offer with no data channel carrying the "mpeg-sd" sub-protocol, and what must it do right after a scene description data channel is successfully established?
reference_answer: If the ITT4RT MRF receives an offer that does not contain a data channel with the "mpeg-sd" sub-protocol, it shall assume the offering ITT4RT client does not support scene description-based overlays. Right after a scene description data channel is successfully established (offer accepted), the ITT4RT MRF shall generate and send the scene description to the offerer.

question: For a PDCH/H in Exclusive MAC mode while in DTM, to which channels must the MS apply the output power ordered on the SACCH, and what is the exception for bursts sent on the BCCH carrier?
reference_answer: For a PDCH/H in Exclusive MAC mode while in DTM, the MS shall apply the output power ordered by the network on the SACCH to all channels, both the TCH/H and the PDCH/H. The exception is that bursts transmitted on the BCCH carrier shall be transmitted at the BCCH level (rather than the SACCH-ordered power).

question: Where in the multiframe is the channel quality measured for the derivation of a Channel Quality Report, and on which carrier is measurement forbidden and why?
reference_answer: Channel quality is measured as the interference signal level during idle frames of the multiframe, when the serving cell is not transmitting. No measurements shall be taken on the BCCH carrier of the serving cell, because the BTS transmits with constant output power on that carrier.

question: When the PCRF links an incoming TDF session to an S9a* session, which address must match, which AVP may supply the PDN information as a secondary criterion, and which annex governs the APN matching?
reference_answer: The PCRF links a TDF session to an S9a* session if the IPv4 address or IPv6 address of the TDF session matches the UE local IP address of the S9a* session. The PDN information (i.e. NSWO-APN), if available in the Called-Station-Id AVP, may also be used as a secondary criterion, and when the PCRF checks whether APNs within Called-Station-Id AVPs match, it shall apply the APN matching procedures in Annex H of 3GPP TS 29.213.

question: How do the PCRF and the HNB GW advertise support for the S15 application after the transport connection comes up, and which two AVP values go inside the Vendor-Specific-Application-Id AVP?
reference_answer: After establishing the transport connection, the PCRF and the HNB GW shall advertise support for the S15 Application by including the application identifier in the Auth-Application-Id AVP and the value 3GPP (10415) in the Vendor-Id AVP, both contained within the Vendor-Specific-Application-Id AVP of the Capabilities-Exchange-Request and Capabilities-Exchange-Answer commands.

question: Which node enforces the default QoS provisioned over Gx for a Fixed Broadband Access IP-CAN session, in which AVP is that default QoS carried, and what does the IP Edge/PCEF not enforce when a PCRF is deployed?
reference_answer: The IP Edge/PCEF enforces the default QoS provisioned over Gx, which is carried in the Default-QoS-Information AVP. When a PCRF is deployed, the IP Edge/PCEF does not enforce the default Access Profile QoS provided by the Broadband Fixed Access Network.

question: When the Extended-Max-Requested-BW-NR feature is supported, which AVPs replace the Max-Requested-Bandwidth-DL/UL AVPs and in what unit do the replacements express the bitrate?
reference_answer: For the Extended-Max-Requested-BW-NR feature, Extended-Max-Requested-BW-DL/UL AVPs shall be used instead of Max-Requested-Bandwidth-DL/UL AVPs, expressing the bitrate in kbps (instead of bps).

question: In the L2TP Session Indications IE, what do the REUIA, REDSA and RENSA bits tell the UP function to request from the LNS?
reference_answer: REUIA (bit 1), if set to "1", indicates to the UP function that it shall request the UE IP address from the LNS. REDSA (bit 2), if set to "1", indicates that the UP function shall request the DNS Server Address from the LNS. RENSA (bit 3), if set to "1", indicates that the UP function shall request the NBNS Server Address from the LNS.

question: Which N1 SM information must a V-SMF place in n1SmInfoFromUe as opposed to unknownN1SmInfo, and what encoding fields must accompany each IE?
reference_answer: The V-SMF shall place NAS SM information it only needs to transfer to the H-SMF — known IEs, and IEs with an unknown value not set to "reserved" that only need forwarding — in n1SmInfoFromUe; it shall place NAS SM information it does not comprehend (unknown IEs, or known IEs with an unknown value not set to "reserved" that the V-SMF is supposed to interpret) in unknownN1SmInfo. Each IE in both cases must be encoded per 3GPP TS 24.501 including the Type field and, for TLV or TLV-E IEs, the Length field.

question: How is the 3gpp-Sbi-Origination-Timestamp header encoded, at what granularity is the time given, and how does its format differ from the ordinary HTTP Date header?
reference_answer: The 3gpp-Sbi-Origination-Timestamp header is encoded per the ABNF in IETF RFC 9110, giving the date and time with millisecond granularity. It uses the same format as the ordinary HTTP Date header but adds milliseconds to the time-of-day (e.g. "Sun, 04 Aug 2019 08:49:37.845 GMT"), whereas the Date header does not include milliseconds.

question: An SMC-CS entity receives a CP-ERROR message while in an arbitrary state. Which two indications must it pass upwards and downwards, and which state must it then enter? How does this differ for an SMC-GP entity?
reference_answer: On receiving a CP-ERROR message, an SMC-CS entity shall pass an error indication to SM-RL and an MM-connection release request to the MM-sublayer, then enter the Idle State. An SMC-GP entity, in contrast, shall only pass an error indication to SM-RL (no MM-connection release request) before entering the Idle State.

question: For an SDP answer whose media line has an unspecified connection address and a visited-realm instance, which clause governs the IMS-ALG's handling, and which one applies when a secondary-realm instance is present instead?
reference_answer: Clause 6.2.5 governs the IMS-ALG's handling when the SDP answer's media line has an unspecified connection address together with a visited-realm instance. Clause 6.2.6 applies when a secondary-realm instance is present instead.

question: An AS receives from a served user an SDP offer that conflicts with an earlier decision to share resources. Which Resource-Share value must go into the response carrying the SDP answer, which header field parameter accompanies it, and what must the AS stop doing?
reference_answer: The response carrying the SDP answer must include a Resource-Share header field set to the value "no-media-sharing", along with the "origin" header field parameter set to "session-initiator" or "session-receiver" as appropriate. The AS must stop applying resource sharing with sessions involving the UE that sent the conflicting request or response.

question: A mobile station receives a short-message control message whose type is not defined for the protocol discriminator. Which CP-ERROR cause value must it return, and which different cause applies when the message type is defined but inconsistent with the protocol state?
reference_answer: The mobile station returns a CP-ERROR message with cause #97 "message type non-existent or not implemented" when the message type is not defined for the protocol discriminator. It returns cause #98 "message type not compatible with the short message protocol state" when the message type is defined but inconsistent with the protocol state.

question: Which bit in the 5GMM capability IE and which bit in the 5GS network feature support IE let the UE and the network respectively declare support for user plane location solutions, and in which registration procedures is that done?
reference_answer: UEs indicate support for user plane location solution(s) using the LCS-UPP bit, the SUPL bit, or both in the 5GMM capability IE. The network indicates its support using the LCS-UPP bit, the SUPL bit, or both in the 5GS network feature support IE. Both indications are done during the initial registration procedure and the mobility registration update procedure.

question: Which identifier must the LMF allocate to tie a UE to an LCS secured user plane connection, what else does the user plane connection information carry, and which message can the UE send to obtain it?
reference_answer: The LMF shall allocate the LCS-UP binding ID to associate the UE with the LCS secured user plane connection. The user plane connection information also carries an address of the LMF. The UE can send the USER PLANE CONNECTION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message to the LMF to obtain the user plane connection information.

question: On the fifth expiry of timer T5010, what must the LMF do with the ongoing LCS-UPP procedures and with the LCS secured user plane connection itself?
reference_answer: On the fifth expiry of timer T5010, the LMF shall abort ongoing LCS-UPP procedures on this LCS secured user plane connection and locally release the LCS secured user plane connection between the UE and the LMF.

question: Under what condition must the Measured Results List IE appear inside the E-CID Measurement Result IE of an E-CID MEASUREMENT REPORT?
reference_answer: The Measured Results List IE shall be included in the E-CID Measurement Result IE of the E-CID MEASUREMENT REPORT message when measurement quantities other than "Default" have been requested.

question: On F1, if a MULTICAST GROUP PAGING message arrives without the UE Identity List for Paging IE, in which paging occasions must the gNB-DU page the MBS session?
reference_answer: If the UE Identity List for Paging IE is absent, the gNB-DU shall perform multicast group paging of the MBS session in all paging occasions within at least one default paging cycle, as specified in TS 38.304.

question: An MCVideo transmission participant receives a Transmission Revoked message whose reason is to queue the transmission. Which message must it send, which timer must it start, and which state must it enter?
reference_answer: It shall send a Queue Position Request message towards the transmission control server, start timer T102 (Transmission Queue Position Request), and enter the 'U: queued transmission' state.

question: Handover with PSCell is commanded from NR SA to EN-DC and the target PSCell is unknown with SMTC configuration present in RRCConnectionReconfiguration. What value does Tprocessing take for a target PSCell in FR2, and what value applies if the target PSCell were known?
reference_answer: When the target PSCell is unknown and SMTC configuration of the target unknown PSCell is present in RRCConnectionReconfiguration, Tprocessing = 50 ms for a target PSCell in FR2. If the target PSCell were known instead, Tprocessing = 45 ms for FR2.

question: In the Dialled Services IP Multimedia CAMEL Subscription Information, how many DP Criteria entries may the list hold, and which item decides whether an IP Multimedia session is released or continued when the IM-SSF to gsmSCF dialogue fails?
reference_answer: The DP Criteria list of the D-IM-CSI may hold 1 to 10 entries. The default Call Handling item decides whether the IP Multimedia session is released or continued in case of error in the IM-SSF to gsmSCF dialogue.

question: Both 3G_MSC-A and 3G_MSC-B support the Multicall supplementary service. After an inter-3G_MSC relocation that already carries one or more circuit connections, are they required to allow a further circuit connection to be set up, and do the establishment procedures differ from the basic case?
reference_answer: Yes, if 3G_MSC-A and 3G_MSC-B support the Multicall supplementary service, a new circuit connection shall be able to be set up after an Inter-3G_MSC relocation that already carries one or more circuit connections. The establishment procedures for the additional circuit connection are the same as those described in clause 13.4.1 (the basic case), so they do not differ.

question: A gNB deployment stores keys in cleartext but is not itself placed in a physically secure location. What must then hold for storage and processing of those keys, and under what condition may a key leave the secure environment?
reference_answer: If a part of a gNB deployment stores or processes keys in cleartext and is not placed in a physically secure location, keys in cleartext shall still be stored and processed in a secure environment. Keys stored inside a secure environment shall never leave that secure environment except when done in accordance with this or other 3GPP specifications.

question: A UE indicates it is capable only of asynchronous dual connectivity. What relative receive timing difference between MCG and SCG subframe timing must it handle, and which inter-band combinations do those requirements cover?
reference_answer: A UE capable only of asynchronous dual connectivity shall be capable of handling a relative receive timing difference between MCG and SCG subframe timing of up to 500 µs. These requirements are only applicable for FDD-FDD inter-band dual connectivity.

question: An NF service consumer PUTs a subscription to UDSF data-change notifications but the resource named in the URI does not exist. What must the UDSF do, which parameter must always be present in the request, and why may the returned expiry attribute differ from the requested one?
reference_answer: If the resource indicated in the URI doesn't exist, the UDSF shall trigger the creation of the subscription. The parameter clientId shall always be included in the request. The returned expiry attribute may differ from the requested one if, due to operator policy, an expiry time is enforced or if the requested value exceeded a maximum allowed expiry time.

question: An announcement must be mixed into an existing media stream of an already established session. Which header field would be used in a re-INVITE, and which 3rd party call control procedure must the AS apply?
reference_answer: A Call-Info header field would be used in the re-INVITE request. The AS must apply the 3rd party call control procedure specified in subclause 5.7.5 of 3GPP TS 24.229.

question: A base station is declared capable of NB-IoT operation in NR in-band. Is it still required to repeat the NR-only transmitter and receiver tests, and which NR resource block position is punctured for the in-band test?
reference_answer: No, a base station declared capable of NB-IoT operation in NR in-band is only required to pass the transmitter and receiver tests for NR with NB-IoT operation in NR in-band; it is not required to perform those tests again for NR only. One NR RB is punctured at the eligible in-band position closest to the NR minimum guard band.

question: For roaming-band TRP conformance of laptop mounted equipment, which two limits must be met (per-channel and aggregate), in which scale must the averaging be done, and which ground plane phantom applies?
reference_answer: The average measured TRP of low, mid and high channel must be higher than the average TRP requirement, and the lowest TRP of each measured channel must be higher than the minimum TRP requirement. Averaging shall be done in linear scale, and the laptop ground plane phantom defined in TR 25.914 subclauses 5.1.3 and 5.1.4 applies.

question: The USIM application toolkit Rejection Cause Code object is populated after a Routing Area Update Reject on UTRAN. Which cause must it carry and how is it coded, and what would it carry instead after an EMM ATTACH REJECT on E-UTRAN?
reference_answer: After a Routing Area Update Reject on UTRAN, the object shall contain the GMM Cause as received in the Routing Area Update Reject message, coded in the same manner as the value part of the GMM Cause information element in TS 24.008. After an EMM ATTACH REJECT on E-UTRAN, it shall instead contain the EMM Cause as received in the EMM ATTACH REJECT message, coded in the same manner as the value part of the EMM Cause information element in TS 24.301.

question: For LSA scenario 2, which entity must let the NM obtain the constraints on cell parameters needed to use LSA spectrum, and which two inputs must the LC take into account when calculating those LSA cell constraints?
reference_answer: The LC shall support a capability allowing the NM to obtain the constraints on cell parameters needed to use LSA spectrum resources. The LC shall take into account LSRAI and the range for cell parameters provided by the NM when calculating the LSA cell constraints.

question: A BSSAP+ receiving entity gets a message whose message type is not defined or not implemented by it. Beyond ignoring the message, what response message must it return and which Gs Cause Value and which IE must that response carry?
reference_answer: It must return a BSSAP+-MOBILE-STATUS message with the Gs Cause Value set to "message unknown" and the Erroneous message IE containing the received message.

question: The IWF floor participant decides to release permission to send media in a broadcast call that was established as a normal call. Which value of the A-bit must the Floor Indicator carry, and what must it include if the earlier Floor Granted message had the G-bit set to 1?
reference_answer: If the session is a broadcast call established as a normal call, the Floor Indicator must carry the A-bit set to '1' (Normal call). If the earlier Floor Granted message had the G-bit set to '1' (Dual floor), the Floor Release message must include the Floor Indicator with the G-bit set to '1' (Dual floor).

question: An IWF floor participant receives a Floor Queue Position Info message whose first subtype bit is set to 1. What must it send back, and which two field values must that response carry?
reference_answer: It must send back a Floor Ack message, which shall include the Message Type field set to '9' (Floor Queue Position Info) and the Source field set to '0' (the IWF floor participant is the source).

question: A UDM invokes the HSS to modify a subscription it created earlier. Which HTTP method must be used and against which resource, and which status code must the HSS return on success?
reference_answer: The HTTP method PATCH must be used, against the URI of the individual subscription resource to be modified. On success, the HSS shall respond with "204 No Content".

question: A UE wants to suspend a data channel media stream that was previously active. Which SDP direction attribute must the invoking UE associate with the corresponding m=application line, and which attribute is used to resume a previously suspended data channel media?
reference_answer: To suspend a previously active data channel media stream, the invoking UE must associate the SDP direction attribute "a=inactive" with the corresponding "m=application" line. To resume a previously suspended data channel media, it uses the SDP direction attribute "a=sendrecv" (or omits the direction attribute) for that line.

question: The CFNR no-reply timer at the IMS AS expires after a 180 (Ringing) response was received. Which requests must the IMS AS send to the diverting UE, whom must it notify, and what must it ask the MF to release?
reference_answer: On no-reply timer expiry, the IMS AS shall send a CANCEL or BYE request to the diverting UE, shall notify the DCSF about the session establishment cancellation or session termination, and shall request the MF to release the allocated data channel media resource on the early dialog of the MMTel session.

question: When sl-ZoneConfig is configured, which formulae must the UE use to determine the Zone_id it is located in, and what does the parameter L correspond to?
reference_answer: The UE uses: x1 = Floor(x / L) Mod 64; y1 = Floor(y / L) Mod 64; Zone_id = y1 * 64 + x1. The parameter L is the value of sl-ZoneLength included in sl-ZoneConfig.

question: For FR1-NTN and FR2-NTN, when the SSB for RLM falls in the same OFDM symbol as a CSI-RS with a different subcarrier spacing and the UE does not support simultaneousRxDataSSB-DiffNumerology, is the UE required to measure both, and what does the specification say about the requirements in that case?
reference_answer: No, the UE is required to measure only one of SSB for RLM and CSI-RS, not both. A longer measurement period for SSB based RLM is expected, and no requirements are defined for that case.

question: Who is obliged to configure the preset enhanced status values for MCData, on what granularity is the configuration applicable, and what minimum and maximum number of possible values must the configuration mechanism allow?
reference_answer: The MCData administrator is obliged to configure the preset enhanced status values, and the configuration is applicable on a per-group basis (part of the MCData group configuration data). The configuration mechanism shall allow a minimum of 32 possible values and up to 65536 separate values.

question: Which reference points must the MCData service use for the procedure of using pre-established MBMS bearers, and may a single such bearer be used by more than one group?
reference_answer: The MCData service shall use the MCData-6, MCData-SDS-1, MCData-SDS-2, MCData-SDS-3, MCData-FD-1, MCData-FD-3, MCData-DS-1 and MCData-DS-3 reference points. Yes, the MBMS bearer can be used by any group.

question: During PC5 unicast establishment between A2X-enabled UEs, must the initiating UE reuse one security context across peer UEs or establish a different one per peer, and which three protections must the PC5 unicast signalling and user plane support?
reference_answer: The initiating UE shall establish a different security context for each peer UE during PC5 unicast establishment if security is activated. The PC5 unicast signalling and user plane shall support confidentiality protection, integrity protection and anti-replay protection.

question: Which two mutually alternative TLS authentication mechanisms must a Remote Device support for key establishment, and what credential must the device be equipped with in each case?
reference_answer: The Remote Device shall support TLS with certificate-based mutual authentication (in which case it shall be equipped with a valid Client Certificate), or shall support shared key based mutual authentication using PSK-TLS (in which case it shall be equipped with a valid pre-shared key).

question: A Remote Device has a stored Ks_local_device key for a UICC Hosting Device but the attempt to use it fails because the UICC Hosting Device does not share that key. What must the Remote Device do next?
reference_answer: The Remote Device shall initiate a new request to the UICC Hosting Device to initiate a new key establishment procedure in order to establish a new Ks_local_device key.

question: An IRPAgent wants to pack multiple notifications into a single push operation. What must it implement so that the IRPManager is not made to wait an objectionable amount of time, what must happen on expiry of that mechanism, and when is it restarted?
reference_answer: The IRPAgent shall implement an IRPAgent-wide timer configurable by the administrator. On expiration of this timer, the IRPAgent shall invoke push if there is at least one notification to be conveyed to the IRPManager. This timer is re-started after each push invocation.

question: A USIM stores a Service Provider Name and the UE is registered on a PLMN that is not the HPLMN and is not one of the PLMN Identifications configured for Service Provider Name display. Which name must be displayed, how many PLMN Identifications must it be possible to associate with the same SP Name, and from which end is the name cut if the UE cannot display it in full?
reference_answer: The PLMN name shall be displayed. It shall be possible to associate at least 10 PLMN Identifications with the same SP Name. If the UE cannot display the full name, it is cut from the tail end.

question: An MCX client obtains an access token to reach an MCX resource server. Which access token type must MCX Connect support, in which HTTP header must the token be carried, and what does the client know about the token itself?
reference_answer: MCX Connect shall initially support the bearer access token type, carried in the HTTP Authorization Header. The access token is opaque to the MCX client, meaning the client has no knowledge of the access token itself (only metadata such as its expiration time).

question: On inter-AMF change or mobility, what must the new AMF acting as NF Service Consumer set in servingNfId and supportedFeatures when it informs the SMF it has taken over the role of serving the UE?
reference_answer: The new AMF (NF Service Consumer) shall set servingNfId to the new serving AMF Id, and shall set the supportedFeatures IE to indicate the features it supports, if at least one feature defined in clause 6.1.8 is supported.

question: What are the permitted approaches a PFCP sender may implement for including the OCI IE towards a receiver, and what obligation does the sender carry regarding propagation delay of overload control information?
reference_answer: The sender may include the OCI IE towards a receiver only when the new/changed value has not already been provided to that receiver; may include the OCI IE in a subset of the messages towards the receiver; or may include the OCI IE periodically (during a first period then cease during a second period), or a combination of these. The sender shall ensure that new/updated overload control information is propagated to the target receivers with an acceptable delay so that effective overload control protection is achieved.

question: When a PFCP node performs message throttling, how must PFCP requests related to eMPS priority traffic and emergency be treated relative to other sessions?
reference_answer: PFCP requests related to eMPS priority traffic and emergency have the highest priority: they shall be the last to be throttled when applying traffic reduction, and shall be exempted from throttling due to PFCP overload control up to the point where the requested traffic reduction cannot be achieved without throttling them.

question: When message prioritization is based on the message priority signalled in the PFCP header, how should a sending PFCP entity determine the relative message priority when the message affects multiple bearers, and what should it set in a Response message?
reference_answer: SEID shall be set to 0 in the PFCP Session Establishment Request message on Sxa/Sxb/Sxc/N4 (and in messages where a peer's SEID is not otherwise available, e.g. certain response/report messages). If a node receives a message for which it has no session (SEID in the PFCP header not known), it shall respond with the "Session context not found" cause.

question: When the PCRF receives service information for a prioritized GC session including a GCSE session indication and service priority level from the GCSE AS, what must it do with the ARP of the derived PCC Rules and of the default bearer?
reference_answer: The PCRF shall derive the PCC Rules for the Group Communication Service and set the ARP (priority level, pre-emption capability, pre-emption vulnerability) of these PCC Rules based on the information received over Rx and operator policies, and shall ensure that the ARP of the default bearer is assigned a prioritized value.

question: When the ProvAFsignalFlow feature is supported and the AF provisions information about AF signalling flows for IMS Restoration, what must the PCF include in the PccRule instances regarding flowInfos and afSigProtocol?
reference_answer: The PCF shall include, within the associated PccRule instance(s), the signalling flows between the UE and the AF within the "flowInfos" attribute, and set the "afSigProtocol" attribute to the value corresponding to the signalling protocol used between the UE and the AF.

question: In the SCPDomainRoutingInfoGet service operation, what does SCP Domain Routing Information with an empty map indicate, and to which document resource must the SCP send the HTTP GET request?
reference_answer: SCP Domain Routing Information with an empty map indicates that no SCP domain is registered in the network (or in the producer NRF for the local request). The SCP shall send the HTTP GET request to the resource URI representing the "scp-domain-routing-info" document resource.

question: In the RANAP Data Volume Report procedure, which IE list must the DATA VOLUME REPORT REQUEST contain, and what must the UTRAN include for each successfully addressed RAB in the DATA VOLUME REPORT message?
reference_answer: The DATA VOLUME REPORT REQUEST must contain the list of RAB ID IEs (RAB Data Volume Report List IE) identifying the RABs for which unsuccessfully transmitted DL data volume shall be reported. For each successfully addressed RAB, the UTRAN must include in the DATA VOLUME REPORT message the Unsuccessfully Transmitted DL Data Volume IE, giving the amount of unsuccessfully transmitted DL data since the last report for that RAB.

question: Upon receipt of the RADIO LINK RECONFIGURATION CANCEL message from the SRNC, what must the DRNS release and which configuration must it continue using?
reference_answer: The DRNS shall release the new configuration previously prepared by the Synchronised RL Reconfiguration Preparation procedure, and continue using the old configuration.

question: When more than one content contribution configuration is provided in the request body of an Update Content Publishing Configuration operation, under what condition is the update successful, and which status code should be returned if the request causes no change?
reference_answer: The update shall be successful if and only if all provided content contribution configurations are acceptable to the Media AF. If the request causes no change to the resource representation, a 204 (No Content) response should be returned.

question: For which domain name and initial path element must the Media Session Handler register itself as URL handler to play the role of 3GPP Service Handler for 5GMS Service URLs?
reference_answer: The Media Session Handler shall register itself as URL handler for the domain name launch.3gppservices.org and the initial path element /ms.

question: If the optional Notification_test_event feature is supported, what must the SCEF do immediately after establishing the notification delivery mechanism when the SCS/AS sets requestTestNotification to true?
reference_answer: The SCEF shall send, immediately after establishing the notification delivery mechanism, a test notification with a body formatted according to the "TestNotification" data type.

question: With the Final-Unit-Indication AVP carrying Final-Unit-Action TERMINATE, what must the Network Element do when the user has consumed the final granted units, and which CC-Request-Type value must the CCR message use to report the Used-Service-Unit AVP?
reference_answer: When the user has consumed the final granted units, the Network Element shall terminate the service. It shall send a CCR message with CC-Request-Type AVP set to UPDATE_REQUEST and report the Used-Service-Unit AVP for the service that has terminated.

question: On sending a 401 Unauthorized response to an unprotected REGISTER request with SIP digest as the security mechanism, which header field parameters must the S-CSCF transport in each WWW-Authenticate header field, and what value must qop take if it is not provided in the authentication vector?
reference_answer: The WWW-Authenticate header field must transport a protection domain in the "realm" parameter, a "nonce" parameter generated by the S-CSCF, an "algorithm" parameter, and a "qop" parameter. If the qop value is not provided in the authentication vector, it shall contain the value "auth".

question: With IMS AKA as the security mechanism, if the S-CSCF receives a REGISTER request with integrity-protected set to yes whose public and private user identities do not match any registered user, which response must it send when it does not support S-CSCF restoration procedures?
reference_answer: The S-CSCF shall respond with a 500 (Server Internal Error) response to the UE.

question: When the UE disables its N1 mode capability for non-3GPP access, what must the UE NAS layer refrain from doing, and what restriction applies to a UE operating in single-registration mode regarding transferring PDN connections?
reference_answer: The UE NAS layer shall not initiate any 5GS NAS procedures towards the network over non-3GPP access. A UE operating in single-registration mode shall not transfer any PDN connection to a non-3GPP access network connected to the 5GCN.

question: How does the controlling MCVideo function determine that a request with the alert-ind element set to false is an authorised MCVideo emergency alert cancellation request, and which element of the ruleset in the MCVideo user profile does it check?
reference_answer: If the <allow-cancel-emergency-alert> element of the <ruleset> element of the MCVideo user profile document identified by the MCVideo ID of the calling user is set to "true", the controlling MCVideo function considers the request an authorised MCVideo emergency alert cancellation request; the function checks the <allow-cancel-emergency-alert> element.

question: If the gNB-CU-UP receives a BEARER CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST containing an E-UTRAN QoS IE for a GBR QoS DRB but the GBR QoS Information IE is not present, how must it report that DRB and in which list of the response?
reference_answer: The gNB-CU-UP shall report the establishment of the corresponding DRB as failed, with an appropriate cause value, in the DRB Failed List IE of the BEARER CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE message.

question: For charging correlation on a session transferred due to STN-SR, which header field parameter must the SCC AS include in the P-Charging-Vector header field of SIP 1xx and 2xx responses, and what must it contain?
reference_answer: The SCC AS shall include the "related-icid" header field parameter, containing the ICID value of the source access leg, in the P-Charging-Vector header field.

question: In the NGAP Uplink RAN Status Transfer procedure, which three IEs must the source NG-RAN node include within the DRBs Subject to Status Transfer List IE for each DRB where PDCP-SN and HFN status preservation applies?
reference_answer: The source NG-RAN node shall include the DRB ID IE, the UL COUNT Value IE, and the DL COUNT Value IE within the DRBs Subject to Status Transfer List IE.
